item.title: More than 80% of thefts in Switzerland involve people with foreign passports.
item.description: 7.956 people convicted of theft last year More than 80% had a foreign passport Approximately 1.500 of those convicted were Swiss Confederation Taskforce
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 7.956 people convicted of theft last year - More than 80% had a foreign passport - Around 1.500 convicted people were Swiss - Confederation and Cantons task force against repeat offenders
## Key facts - Convicted of theft → 7,956 last year - Nationality in statistics → indicated from 2024 - Swiss convicts → approximately 1,500 - Foreign passport → over 80% - Permanent resident population → approximately two thirds of those convicted with foreign passports are not part of it
### The photograph of the convictions Last year 7,956 people were convicted of theft in Switzerland. It is the central data of the new statistics on criminal sentences from the Confederation, which places thefts alongside road crimes among the categories that collect a large part of the convictions. The data was reported by SRF. The shortening of the days marks the start of the apartment burglary season.
ZHAW criminologist Dirk Baier considers the figure high, but not unexpected. In the SRF «Tagesschau», he defined theft as a significant and often underestimated area of ​​crime.
> In essence, theft represents a significant area of ​​crime, but it often remains underestimated.
Crime statistics also show that two thirds of crimes are property crimes. Examples include bicycle theft, bag theft and burglary.
### Nationality and residence From 2024 the statistics indicate the nationality of those convicted for each crime. In the case of the thefts, around 1,500 convicted people were Swiss, while more than 80% had foreign passports. Among the nationalities particularly represented are those of Algeria and Romania. Furthermore, approximately two-thirds of those convicted with foreign passports are not part of the permanent resident population.
Finally, the source distinguishes two groups indicated by Baier: asylum seekers and criminal tourists. For the former, it recalls a situation that may include few prospects and little money; for the latter it talks about people who arrive in Switzerland knowing that objects are not always well protected and that attention may be insufficient. According to the SEM, the Confederation and the cantons have set up a taskforce for the asylum sector. With regard to repeat offenders, the taskforce uses every instrument provided by law to detain them until their departure. However, the SEM specifies that only a small minority of asylum seekers commit crimes. The Federal Council expects further tightening of the asylum procedure. ## Three filters for reading the statistics
For people living in Switzerland, the number acquires a precise meaning only if three elements are considered together: the alleged offense, the judicial outcome and the nationality indicator. The short formula in the headline does not replace the complete data.
### Conviction, passport, residence
The first filter is the word convicted. The 7.956 people are presented in the Confederation's new criminal judgments statistics as having been convicted of theft last year. The total should therefore be cited with this category. The source places thefts and traffic offenses among the largest categories of convictions, but does not turn the number of people convicted of theft into a general total for crime.
The second filter concerns the passport. More than 80% of those convicted of theft had a foreign passport, while around 1.500 were Swiss. The indication of nationality for each offense is a new feature of the statistics as of 2024. Algeria and Romania are identified as particularly represented nationalities, without the text reporting the number of people convicted for each. The correct wording therefore remains what is available: a particularly strong presence, not a numerical ranking.
The third filter is residence. Around two thirds of those convicted with a foreign passport are not part of the permanent resident population. Passport and permanent residence thus describe two different elements of the same data. For a national reading, this distinction prevents the two categories from being automatically conflated.
| Element | Source data | Practical reading | |---|---|---| | Offense | Theft | The number concerns this offense | | Nationality | Indicated since 2024 | The comparison uses the passport | | Residence | Around two thirds outside the permanent resident population | It is a separate indicator |
The same caution is needed when discussing public responses. Baier distinguishes asylum seekers and criminal tourists; SEM reports a task force established by the Confederation and Cantons for the asylum sector and emphasizes that only a small minority of asylum seekers commit crimes. The task force is described as operational with regard to repeat offenders, while the further tightening measures are still attributed to the Federal Council's plans. The source indicates neither a date nor the content of such tightening measures. The reader can therefore distinguish what is presented as an established measure from what is presented as a political forecast. For aspects unrelated to criminal statistics, costo della vita in Svizzera should be consulted separately.

## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to check the data before using it
### Practical sequence for the reader
A reader who comes across a headline on the subject can verify the news by following the source’s sequence, without adding unpublished numbers or categories.
1. Identify the measure. Ask whether the number concerns people convicted of theft in Switzerland, as in the figure of 7.956 convictions from last year. 2. Check the period. The source refers to last year and specifies that nationality has been indicated for each offense since 2024. These indications must not be replaced with a different date. 3. Separate the figures. About 1.500 convicted persons were Swiss; over 80% had a foreign passport. These are the two numerical pieces of information available for comparison, to be reported together. 4. Add residence. About two thirds of those convicted with a foreign passport were not part of the permanent resident population. This step avoids presenting a passport as synonymous with residence. 5. Distinguish the responses. For the asylum sector, SEM indicates a task force of the Confederation and the cantons. Regarding repeat offenders, it uses every legal possibility to detain them until their departure; the Federal Council, on the other hand, plans further tightening of the asylum procedure.
This sequence is not an administrative procedure for someone who has suffered a theft: the text does not indicate forms, offices to contact, deadlines or instructions for citizens and residents. It is a way to avoid confusing statistics, groups and measures. The reader may also remember that SEM describes the minority of asylum seekers who commit crimes as small, while Baier points out difficulties in countermeasures against criminal tourists. This distinction too belongs to the source and does not warrant broader conclusions about people with foreign passports.

item.title: Expensive PCs and smartphones: AI is absorbing chips
item.description: Price increases ranging from 40% to 120% reported by MediaMarkt.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - AI absorbs RAM and memory allocated to data centers - In Switzerland, some models are unavailable or much more expensive - MediaMarkt reports average price increases of 40% to 120% - Interdiscount expects stable availability in the coming months
## Key facts - Cause → global demand for RAM and storage systems - Products → notebooks, desktop PCs, tablets and smartphones - Fust → growing scarcity since mid-2026 - MediaMarkt → procurement difficulties since late 2025 - Prices → average increases of 40% to 120% since the start of the chip crisis - Interdiscount → sporadic shortages of processors and high-capacity memory
In Lugano, anyone who has saved money for a new mobile phone or needs to retire their laptop may face two problems: the model is unavailable, or the configuration with more memory costs several hundred francs more. The difficulty affects stores and online platforms, and the phenomenon has also reached Switzerland.
The explanation given is global: the strong expansion of data centers dedicated to artificial intelligence is absorbing RAM and storage systems. Demand for these components is said to be driven by the growth of AI, while an increasing share of production is said to be destined for data centers and the infrastructure they require. For PCs, notebooks and other devices, the result is less certain availability, with repercussions for the choice of models and configurations.
### A problem that starts with the components
Retailers describe a situation that is not uniform. Interdiscount reports sporadic shortages of certain processors and high-capacity memory modules across the market. The difficulty varies depending on the model and configuration; according to the company, the most delicate point is the dynamics of supply and prices. The forecast communicated is for stable availability in the coming months.
Fust reports observing, since mid-2026, growing scarcity of notebooks, desktop PCs and devices with high memory capacities. It does not yet speak of a general interruption, but of longer restocking times and rising prices.
MediaMarkt dates the difficulties to late 2025. The first reports, it explains, concerned Windows OEM manufacturers and then Apple. In its assessment, the problem is not limited to notebooks and PCs: it also includes smartphones. For those looking for a phone, comparing offerte mobile therefore does not replace checking the device's availability.
The three responses show a non-uniform market: for some components, the shortage remains sporadic; for others, lead times are getting longer, while price pressure is affecting more categories. The situation affects notebooks, desktop PCs, tablets and smartphones, but with intensity linked to the configuration. For Swiss consumers, the comparison cannot stop at the device name. Retailers' responses link availability and price to manufacturer, model, processor, memory and configuration. The same product family can therefore present different conditions when the required capacity changes.
### Capacity becomes the decisive variable
MediaMarkt observes that those who only want to browse online and reply to emails often do not need 16 GB of RAM. Likewise, for many uses, a 256 or 512 GB SSD may be sufficient instead of 1 TB. The assessment should be made before paying the premium for a higher-capacity configuration, without automatically considering the minimum capacity suitable for every need.
Companies are reacting in different ways. Interdiscount focuses on forward-looking planning and alternative configurations. Fust speaks of proactive inventory management, diversification among distributors and advance volume planning; if a model is unavailable, it proposes equivalent alternative configurations. MediaMarkt orders larger quantities in advance because it expects price increases on a quarterly basis, thereby maintaining more advantageous prices for a longer period.
For buyers, the practical consequence is that the alternative is not simply to wait or give up. You can ask whether the problem concerns the exact model, the processor, the RAM or the SSD storage, and assess an equivalent configuration. This distinction is also relevant for smartphones, which MediaMarkt includes among the affected products.
The time factor should also be viewed with caution. Interdiscount expects stable availability in the coming months; Fust, on the other hand, reports significantly longer restocking times and rising prices. MediaMarkt links its ordering policy to quarterly price increases. These indications do not produce a single answer valid for everyone: waiting may mean finding more choice according to one forecast, but it does not guarantee spending less.
The responses collected do not indicate a certain window for Black Friday or Cyber Monday and do not set a purchase date valid for everyone. For a family or a worker, the expense must therefore be included in planning for costo della vita in Svizzera: the price to compare is that of the configuration actually needed, not that of the highest-capacity model seen online.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. The most practical way to approach the market described by the retailers is to turn the research into a configuration check, rather than a hunt for the commercial name alone. The process can be applied to notebooks, desktop PCs, tablets and smartphones, categories mentioned in the responses.
### Five checks before ordering
1. Start with the actual use. If the need is to browse online and respond to emails, consider MediaMarkt's indication regarding configurations with 16 GB of RAM and a 1 TB SSD. The assessment should be made before settling on a higher capacity.
2. Write down the requirements for the model you are looking for: processor, RAM, SSD capacity and overall configuration. The shortages reported by Interdiscount in fact vary precisely according to the model and configuration.
3. Check availability both in stores and online. A model may not be available in a specific configuration, while the retailer may offer an alternative. Therefore, do not stop at the series name: check the device's complete specifications.
4. If the exact configuration is not available, ask for an equivalent proposal. Interdiscount indicates alternative configurations, Fust equivalent alternatives and MediaMarkt also simpler configurations to keep products in different price ranges.
5. Compare the timing of the purchase with the signals from the retailers. Interdiscount expects stable availability over the coming months; Fust reports longer lead times and rising prices; MediaMarkt orders in advance in anticipation of quarterly increases. These are factors to consider alongside the price of the chosen configuration.
Before concluding, note down the model, processor, RAM, storage space, price and availability. The same check applies to a smartphone, because MediaMarkt also includes this category among the supply difficulties. This way, the search remains anchored to the features that are genuinely necessary and not merely to the highest capacity offered.
If you want to relate the expense to your personal budget, complete the check with calcolatore stipendio.

## TL;DR - The calendar provides for four federal voting days every year - A federal initiative requires 100'000 signatures collected over a period of 18 months - An optional referendum requires 50'000 signatures within 100 days - Constitutional amendments must obtain the double majority of the people and the Cantons
## Key facts - Scope → cantonal vote in the Canton of Lucerne - Federal calendar → four voting dates per year - Federal popular initiative → 100'000 signatures in 18 months - Optional federal referendum → 50'000 signatures in 100 days - Constitutional amendment → majority of the people and the Cantons
### The level of the consultation
There are four federal voting dates scheduled each year: this is the first reference point to keep separate when consulting a guide to cantonal voting in the Canton of Lucerne. The federal calendar provides the national framework; the date and instructions for the cantonal vote should be read in the Canton’s official information.
The second step is to identify the instrument. Within the federal framework, a popular initiative requires 100'000 signatures collected in 18 months, while an optional referendum requires 50'000 signatures in 100 days. These are federal thresholds and deadlines. They should therefore not be used automatically to describe the cantonal procedure: for Lucerne, the applicable rule is the one given in the official information about the vote.
If the proposal amends the Constitution, the indicated federal framework provides for a double majority: both the people and the Cantons must vote in favor. This criterion must also be read together with the level of the vote, because a cantonal guide must distinguish the applicable instrument from the general federal rule.
To interpret the content, it is useful to link each topic to the competent administration. The Swiss tax system has three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal taxes and municipal taxes. The AFC/ESTV is responsible for direct federal tax and VAT; the cantonal administrations oversee cantonal and municipal taxation. In municipalities, the multiplier is applied to the cantonal tax.
The same criterion avoids other misunderstandings. The UST/BFS produces statistics and does not set tax rates. The UFAS/BSV concerns social security, including AVS/AHV, AI and LPP/BVG, and does not set taxes. The LAMal/KVG, on the other hand, is compulsory health insurance for residents: it must be taken out within three months of arrival, has per-capita premiums and is neither a tax nor a wage contribution.
To assess the possible impact on a family, reading the question can be supplemented with the guide on costo della vita in Svizzera. The tool helps organize expenditure items; the voting decision must remain anchored in the text and the official information about the vote. ## Practical effects to distinguish
A guide to a cantonal vote is more useful when it connects the subject of the consultation to the rule that the reader needs to verify. Not all matters that affect daily life belong to the same level: a tax item, an insurance premium, an employment relationship and a rent follow different frameworks.
### The subject-matter grid
| Subject | Checkpoint | | Fisco | The AFC/ESTV administers direct federal tax and VAT; for cantonal and municipal taxation, the cantonal administrations are authoritative. The municipality applies its own multiplier to cantonal tax. | | LAMal/KVG | For residents, it is mandatory and must be taken out within three months of arrival. Premiums are per capita and vary by canton or region; cantonal premium reductions are available. It is neither a tax nor a payroll contribution. | | Work | There is no federal minimum wage, but some Cantons provide for their own. The ordinary limit is 45 hours per week for industry, offices and retail and 50 hours in other sectors; minimum holidays amount to four weeks, or five for those under 20. | | Tenancy | CO art. 253 et seq. constitutes federal law, the same in every canton. The security deposit may not exceed three months' rent and must be deposited in a blocked account in the tenant's name; the landlord must use the official cantonal form for termination, which can be challenged within 30 days before the conciliation authority. |
The comparison prevents reading an item of healthcare expenditure as if it were automatically a tax. LAMal premiums depend on the canton and region, while premium reduction is a cantonal subsidy; adult deductibles are indicated at levels of CHF 300, 500, 1'000, 1'500, 2'000 and 2'500. The distinction matters because LAMal is not a contribution withheld from wages.
For a work-related topic, the practical question is whether it concerns a federal rule or a cantonal minimum wage; the absence of a federal minimum does not automatically become valid information for every Canton. For housing, by contrast, the federal nature of tenancy rules coexists with an official cantonal form for the landlord's termination notice. The procedure to follow therefore depends on the precise subject, not merely on the fact that the vote is being held in Lucerne.
The same applies to social assistance and the public services mentioned. Their administration is generally cantonal or municipal, and the conditions must be verified with the competent office. If the topic concerns health insurance premiums, confronto LAMal e cassa malati can help interpret the expenditure item without confusing it with payroll contributions.

## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## Practical procedure before voting
### Five checks before casting your vote
1. Start with the official calendar. Look for the information from the Canton of Lucerne concerning the consultation and note the date given for the cantonal vote. The federal and cantonal calendars should be kept separate. 2. Identify the instrument. Mark whether the text concerns an initiative or referendum. Federal thresholds and deadlines should not be automatically applied to Lucerne: use the rules specified for that level. 3. Verify who is entitled to vote. Use the official guidance linked to the vote to verify who may vote and how the procedure is described. Do not fill in missing data with generic rules. 4. Determine the area of responsibility. For taxes, distinguish direct federal tax, cantonal taxes and municipal taxes; for VAT and IFD, consider AFC/ESTV; for AVS/AHV, AI and LPP/BVG, consider UFAS/BSV. UST/BFS is used for statistics, not tax rates. 5. Check the correct deadline. The three-month period under LAMal runs from arrival; the 30 days concern challenging the termination of a lease. These are deadlines distinct from the official voting date and must not be confused.
A simple method is to note three columns: fact reported in the official information, competent level and practical consequence to be checked. The first column includes the wording of the question and the calendar; the second, the federal, cantonal or municipal administration indicated by the subject matter; the third, any item concerning taxes, premiums, work, rent or public service. This sheet prevents using a UST/BFS statistic as a tax rate or attributing the setting of a tax to UFAS/BSV.
If the consultation concerns taxes, dichiarazione delle imposte may serve to link the subject matter to your own situation, but it does not replace the official instructions. If it concerns a cantonal competence, requirements, deadlines and amounts must be verified with the Canton’s official source, as required for services administered at that level.

item.description: The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics will be announced on October 12 Ernst Fehr is among the possible winners Clarivate has identified four economists Polymarket estimates Fehr
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences will be announced on October 12 - Ernst Fehr is among the possible winners - Clarivate has named four economists - Polymarket estimates Fehr at 6%
## Key facts - Prize → 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics - Announcement → Monday, October 12 - Candidate → Ernst Fehr, Swiss-Austrian economist - Polymarket → Ariel Pakes 19%, Ernst Fehr 6% - Institute → UBS International Center of Economics in Society - Academic recognition → USI honorary doctorate in 2009
The winner of the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics will be announced on Monday, October 12. Ernst Fehr, a Swiss-Austrian economist and professor at the University of Zurich, remains among the possible recipients.
The 70-year-old has been considered a possible winner for years, but is not among the leading favorites. Predicting the choice remains difficult: the Nobel Foundation keeps the names of the candidates secret, and decisions from previous years offer few clues about the committee's intentions.
### The scientific profile
Fehr is one of the leading figures in behavioral economics, which examines the processes underlying individual economic decisions. His studies have helped cast doubt on the traditional model of “Homo oeconomicus,” which portrays individuals as guided exclusively by self-interest.
The studies cited by the source show instead that fairness, justice and the well-being of others also factor into choices. For this reason, Fehr is among the most cited economists in the German-speaking world.
Since 2012, he has headed the UBS International Center of Economics in Society, an institute affiliated with the University of Zurich and established thanks to an initial funding of 100 million Swiss francs from UBS bank. Fehr has assured that the institute's scientific independence is “completely guaranteed.”
His relationship with the Swiss university system also includes Università della Svizzera italiana: in 2009, USI awarded him an honorary doctorate.
His international reputation was on display last June: a conference held in Zurich to celebrate his 70th birthday was attended by several Nobel laureates, including Abhijit Banerjee, Esther Duflo, Joel Mokyr, Oliver Hart and Jean Tirole.
Clarivate did not include the economist among the names highlighted for 2026. The company selects researchers based on the scientific impact reflected in citations of their work; the source nevertheless specifies that the list does not constitute an official prediction of the award.
The picture therefore remains open, with Fehr still among the possible winners but outside the group of leading favorites. The decision will be made public only with the announcement scheduled for Monday, October 12.
Unlike the other five Nobel Prizes, this award was not provided for in Alfred Nobel's will. For the Swiss public, the point is not to turn every signal into a prediction, but to distinguish the sources accompanying the race for the prize. The source presents three: Clarivate's selection, the Polymarket prediction market, and the announcement by the Nobel committee.
### Three signals, three levels of reliability
| Signal | Reported data | Correct interpretation | |---|---|---| | Clarivate | Michael Woodford, Columbia University, monetary theory and central bank communication; Susan Athey, Stanford, and Hal Varian, Berkeley, economics of information technologies; Sidney Winter, Pennsylvania, evolutionary economics and firms' adaptation. | Unofficial selection | | Polymarket | Ariel Pakes, Harvard, 19%; Ernst Fehr, sixth, 6%. | Speculative assessments, not the committee's decision | | Announcement | Monday, October 12, winner of the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences. | Outcome to await |
Clarivate's list brings together names selected on the basis of scientific impact measured by citations. Therefore, Fehr's absence does not amount to a rejection, and the presence of the four economists does not amount to an official shortlist from the Nobel committee.
The second signal comes from a market in which users can bet on the award. Ariel Pakes, a Harvard economist specializing in empirical market analysis, is listed at 19%; Fehr is sixth at 6%. The source describes these assessments as speculative: they do not necessarily reflect the committee's decision.
For those reading the news from Switzerland, this distinction avoids assigning excessive meaning to a percentage. The 6% describes the position indicated by Polymarket at that moment, not an official figure from the Nobel Foundation nor an outcome already decided.
The possible award for studies on the digital economy introduces another perspective. Clarivate links Athey and Varian to the economics of information technologies; recognition in this area would be significant given the growing importance of online platforms, data, and artificial intelligence. The source, however, presents it as a possibility.
The national link remains primarily academic and institutional: the candidate teaches in Zurich, directs the center associated with the university, and has received an honorary doctorate from USI. No measure for families, businesses, or workers is announced.
Those who want to supplement their reading of the prize with more everyday indicators can consult costo della vita in Svizzera, keeping service data separate from news about the scientific recognition.

To follow the announcement without confusing candidacy, prediction, and result, a brief procedure can be applied. Its main purpose is to establish which information is already available and which remains to be verified.
### A five-step check
1. Set the verification date. Monday, October 12 is the deadline indicated by the source for knowing the winner of the 2026 Nobel Prize in Economics. Before then, use phrases such as possible winner or favorite, not winner.
2. Identify the origin of the names. If the list comes from Clarivate, read it as a selection based on publication citations, not as a communication from the Nobel Foundation.
3. Treat the percentages separately. If Polymarket appears, remember that the figures 19% and 6% are estimates from the prediction market: the first concerns Ariel Pakes, the second Ernst Fehr.
4. Check the language of the headline. The source allows Fehr to be described as a candidate or possible winner; it does not allow anticipating the committee's choice based on his position or the Clarivate list.
5. After the announcement, compare only the communicated outcome with the previous predictions. In this way, a market estimate and a citation-based selection remain different categories even when they point to the same name.

Therefore, no personal deadline to meet or document to submit emerges. Its practical usefulness is to help read a Swiss economic news item precisely, without turning it into a measure that the source does not announce.
The reference to UBS should also be kept within its proper scope: in the source, it concerns the initial contribution to the center directed by Fehr and its scientific independence. It is not presented as an instruction for the reader. For different needs, the guide to conti bancari in Svizzera can be consulted; it belongs to a separate operational plan.

## TL;DR - In Lucerne, work does not begin before the permit. - The procedure involves the municipality and canton. - Documents, objections and appeals are part of the process.
## Key facts - Scope → building permit in the Canton of Lucerne - Parties → municipality and canton - Steps → documents, objections or appeals - Constraint → prohibition on starting work before the permit
In the Canton of Lucerne, a building permit is the step that precedes the start of construction work. The practical rule indicated for this procedure is clear-cut: work must not begin before the permit has been issued. It is therefore not enough to have a project ready or to have prepared the documentation; commencement remains subject to authorization.
The procedure concerns four points that the applicant must address together: understanding when the permit is required, preparing the documents, identifying the role of the municipality and the canton, and handling any objections or appeals. These are connected elements, but they cannot replace one another. An application focused solely on the project, for example, leaves the administrative step uncovered; a formally submitted application, on the other hand, does not authorize bringing forward the construction schedule.
### The institutional framework
The municipality and the canton appear in the procedure with roles that must be considered separately. For those who live or work in Switzerland, this means that a procedure in the Canton of Lucerne must be understood within the relevant cantonal and municipal framework, without automatically importing requirements or steps from another canton. The framework includes both levels—municipality and canton—and requires following the process through them.
The documentation must also be treated as part of the application, not as a secondary attachment. The operational objective is to submit everything required by the procedure applicable to the application, checking the channel indicated by the competent offices. It is not correct to turn a generic list into a universal rule, because what must be ascertained is the procedure applicable to the intervention.
The possibility of objections or appeals completes the framework. Before considering the process complete, the applicant must know whether the application is still in the administrative phase and whether these instruments have been activated. The prohibition on starting work before the permit remains the reference point even when project planning is already advanced. The sequence must therefore be built around the permit, not only around the work to be carried out. The practical problem is not simply filling out an application. It is coordinating timings and decisions without confusing the authorization with project preparation. For anyone assessing an intervention, the useful comparison is between two scenarios: before the permit and after the permit. In the first, documents and communications can be organized, but work cannot begin. In the second, the application has passed the authorization step indicated by the procedure, and one enters the next phase provided for by that decision.
### Three checks that prevent errors
The first check concerns whether authorization is required. Not all assessments can start from the same premise, because the central question is when the permit is required. If this point remains open, the construction schedule is also exposed to an error: scheduling the start before clarifying the required authorization. The prudent choice, consistent with the stated prohibition, is to keep work on hold until the authorization is available.
The second concerns documentation. Preparing documents does not simply mean collecting attachments; it means linking them to the application that the municipality and canton must examine. An organized file helps follow the procedure, but does not allow official instructions to be replaced with a template taken from another Canton. Requirements, deadlines and offices for building permits follow cantonal rules: for Lucerne, the operational reference is the canton's official source.
The third check concerns objections and appeals. These instruments should not be treated as an aside: they may become the point to clarify before considering the process ready for the construction site. Without inventing deadlines or authorities not indicated, the concrete question is which administrative phase has been reached before organizing the construction site.
This method is also useful for the family budget. The same principle applies to a project overseen by people who work in another Canton: the rule to apply remains that of the Canton competent for the procedure.

To turn the keyword into an operational sequence, the process can be organized into six steps. The first is to describe the work precisely and verify whether it falls among the cases in which a building permit is required in the Canton of Lucerne. Until this point is clarified, the start of the work must not be scheduled.
The second step is to identify the correct channel between the municipality and the canton. The application should not be addressed based on practices developed elsewhere: the reference is the applicable cantonal procedure and the role assigned to the municipality. The verification must be carried out using the canton’s official source, because building permits, requirements, deadlines and offices follow cantonal rules.
### From application to decision
Third: prepare the required documents. The specific list depends on the application to be submitted and should not be completed with generic templates or invented attachments. Fourth: submit the application through the indicated channel, keeping the municipal and cantonal levels separate. ## TL;DR - Late September: attack on Publica's software provider - Names, AHV numbers and salaries among the data at risk - Publica has 66’000 active insured persons and 40’000 pension recipients - Pension funds were not affected
## Key facts - Institution → Publica, the Swiss Confederation's pension fund - Provider → PK Softech AG - Timing → late September - Potentially affected → approximately 66’000 active insured persons and 40’000 pension beneficiaries - Investigation → Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland - Funds → not affected and safe, according to Publica
At the end of September, a cyberattack hit an external software provider of Publica, the Swiss Confederation's pension fund. The incident caused a data breach and, according to current findings, may have involved particularly sensitive personal information.
The case became public on Thursday, after Publica sent a notice to the insured. The document, seen by SRF, indicates that personal data were probably stolen. Beatrice Rychen, spokesperson for the pension institution, described what happened in stark terms: «For us, this is the worst thing that could have happened».
The information that may have been obtained includes first and last names, dates of birth, AHV numbers, addresses, private and business telephone numbers, as well as personal and business email addresses. The list also includes pension data, such as salary and pension assets, marital status and information relating to a spouse or partner.
### The route via the external provider
It is not yet clear whether the leak concerns all approximately 66’000 active insured persons and 40’000 pension beneficiaries, or only some of them. Publica does clarify, however, that the pension funds were not affected and are safe.
The cybercriminals did not attack the Swiss Confederation's pension fund directly. The target was PK Softech AG, the external company that develops applications for pension funds. Through this provider, the perpetrators are believed to have gained access to Publica's data.
The Office of the Attorney General of Switzerland is investigating the case. In the meantime, specialists are analyzing the stolen information. It is not known whether the attack also involved data from other pension institutions. For anyone checking their own situation, the AHV number entry is therefore one of the categories to distinguish from investments and funds, which Publica says were not affected. The guide on previdenza AVS may help with navigating pension terminology. ### Two distinct risks for insured persons
The matter has two distinct dimensions. The first concerns the possible theft of personal data; the second concerns pension funds. Publica says the funds are safe, while warning of a risk to individuals linked to the misuse of the information.
The theft of a name, address, AHV number, salary or pension assets could, according to the institution, be used in an attempt to assume other people's identities or to gain an advantage. The risk mentioned does not, however, mean that unlawful use of the data has already been established. Specialists are still analyzing how much was stolen.
| Scenario | What the source indicates | Practical interpretation | |---|---|---| | Only some of the insured persons are involved | The scope has not been clarified | Not everyone affected would necessarily be exposed | | All insured persons and beneficiaries are involved | The possibility has not been ruled out | The scope would be broader, but this has not been confirmed | | Pension funds | Publica says they are safe | The news concerns data, not a declared loss of funds |
The reference to salary also makes it important to interpret correctly any salary information that may be contained in the stolen data. For this reason, it may be useful to consult busta paga svizzera, without confusing a category of personal data with a movement in the pension account.
The attack bears similarities to the one that involved Xplain in 2023: in that case, cybercriminals had gained access to information from federal offices through an external software company, resulting in the theft of approximately 1,3 million sensitive files. Two years ago, at the end of an administrative investigation, the Federal Council had adopted measures to prevent further thefts at IT providers. Since then, cooperation with external companies has also been subject to additional security requirements.
The precedent does not automatically make it possible to determine the scope of the Publica case. It does, however, show why the software provider, although not the Confederation's pension fund, is the central focus of the investigation.

## TL;DR - Thirteen disruptions on the line since the beginning of the year - Over 150’000 passengers and more than 700 trains every day - Burnt cables, damaged tracks and a bird among the causes - Léman 2030 expands the stations in Lausanne and Geneva
## Key facts - Line → Geneva-Fribourg - Disruptions → thirteen since the beginning of the year - Daily traffic → over 150’000 passengers and more than 700 trains - Causes → burnt cables, damaged tracks, short circuit caused by a bird - Programme → Léman 2030 - New line → Morges-Perroy
Thirteen disruptions since the beginning of the year have affected the railway line between Geneva and Fribourg. Each incident started with a failure at a strategic point and halted traffic on a route that carries over 150’000 passengers every day and sees more than 700 trains pass through.
The causes of the incidents varied: cables caught fire, tracks were damaged and a bird even caused a short circuit. For passengers, however, the outcome was similar: delays and cancellations, with few alternatives when the line is blocked. The frustration, the source reports, is palpable among those who say they have already experienced several service disruptions.
### The reliability bottleneck
Among the incidents mentioned are the track damage attributed to the Servette ultras in Lausanne. The case adds to a sequence in which the source of the problem changes, while the consequence for rail traffic remains the same. For those who need to plan a journey, the issue is therefore not only the technical cause of the failure, but also the difficulty of quickly finding a replacement for the route.
The pressure is also evident on board. During peak hours, it is not always possible to find a seat; in the morning and evening, trains are often full. The line thus combines two distinct problems: disruption when a failure occurs and overcrowding when the service continues.
According to FFS, not all disruptions are caused by its operations. Linus Looser, Head of Infrastructure at Swiss Federal Railways, explains: > «Every day, the line sees over 150’000 passengers and more than 700 trains pass through. Disruptions are no more frequent than elsewhere, but they have a greater impact: without alternative routes, a single failure can bring the entire line to a standstill and have a major impact on customers.»
Over the past twenty years, the number of passengers has tripled. The infrastructure response includes the Léman 2030 programme, with the expansion of the stations in Lausanne and Geneva, and the new line between Morges and Perroy, the first step towards greater capacity between Lausanne and Geneva. For those consulting mezzi pubblici, the article therefore describes a route where demand, overcrowding and vulnerability of rail traffic combine. ## What changes for those who use the route
The practical reading of the situation starts with a distinction: reliability and capacity are related but not identical problems. A fault at a strategic point can bring the line to a standstill because there are not enough alternative routes; when the trains are running, however, the number of passengers and the growth recorded translate into trains that are often full. Solving one problem does not automatically eliminate the other.
### Three pressures to separate
| Pressure | Source data | Described consequence | |---|---|---| | Disruptions | thirteen since the beginning of the year | delays and cancellations | | Network without alternatives | a single fault can block the entire line | major impact on customers | | Demand | passengers tripled in twenty years | more pressure on the route |
The table helps read the risk without confusing an incident with the underlying trend. The causes listed are different, from burnt cables to a short circuit caused by a bird, but the traveler experiences the same operational problem when service comes to a halt. The frequency indicated by the source is not enough on its own to describe the daily burden: the lack of alternatives and the crowding of trains during peak hours also matter.
For those who use the route, the concrete consequence is greater exposure to two scenarios. In the first, a delay or cancellation disrupts the travel itinerary, and changing routes is not necessarily possible. In the second, the train departs but a seat is not guaranteed, especially in the morning and evening. These are different conditions, and the infrastructure response must take both into account.
### Investments and the pace of demand
The Léman 2030 program and the Morges-Perroy line show that the increase in passenger numbers requires more capacity. The source links the new line to the expansion between Lausanne and Geneva and mentions the expansion of the stations in Lausanne and Geneva. However, it does not present these works as an immediate solution to every disruption between Geneva and Fribourg. The distinction is useful: more seats and greater capacity concern structural pressure, while a blockage caused by a fault remains a service continuity problem. The mezzi pubblici must therefore also be assessed on both levels: the ability to travel and the reliability of the route.

1. Identify whether the journey concerns the line between Geneva and Fribourg. It is the route at the center of the thirteen interruptions recorded since the beginning of the year. 2. Consider the time slot. In the morning and evening, trains are often full, so a seat is not guaranteed during peak hours. 3. Keep the two risks separate: a crowded train does not mean that a line is interrupted, while a breakdown at a strategic point can bring traffic to a standstill. 4. In the event of a disruption, do not assume that an immediate alternative route exists. The source notes that the absence of alternatives can block the entire line and increase the impact on customers. 5. Read the long-term projects: Léman 2030 concerns the expansion of the stations in Lausanne and Geneva; Morges-Perroy is indicated as the first step toward increasing capacity between Lausanne and Geneva.

item.description: 80% of the vacant positions are filled by local staff.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 80% of vacancies are filled by local staff. - Direct hiring from abroad accounts for about 20%. - Family accommodation with a home office can cost 6000 CHF. - In urban centers, vacant housing is extremely scarce.
## Key facts - Vacant positions filled locally → 80% - Direct hires from abroad → approximately 20% - Interviewee → Christian Atkinson - Company → Robert Walters - Family accommodation with a home office → can quickly reach 6000 francs per month - City of residence → Zurich
80% of vacancies in Switzerland are filled by local staff. Christian Atkinson, who coordinates Robert Walters' Swiss personnel consultancy activities, emphasizes this to put into perspective the idea that companies primarily look across the border for highly qualified professionals.
According to the headhunter, when a company has to fill a position, it starts with the domestic market. It looks for people already rooted in the country, with suitable qualifications and knowledge of the local work culture. Direct hires from abroad perhaps account for 20%. For the employer, the risk is real: a candidate may withdraw at the last moment, visa procedures may drag on, or integration may not work. In that case, whoever has arrived leaves at the first opportunity.
The high salary remains an attraction, but it is not enough to explain the choice. Atkinson describes an enormous costo della vita in Svizzera capable of reducing the salary advantage. After the first bills for rent and health insurance, actual savings may turn out to be almost the same as those attainable, for example, in the United Kingdom. For this reason, anyone who changes jobs exclusively for the salary is, in his view, a warning sign.
### Rent, family and first impressions
Housing is now companies' main concern and the most stressful factor for those who want to relocate. In urban centers, the vacancy rate is extremely low; many expats have to move several times during the first few months. For a family, an apartment with a dedicated home office space can quickly cost up to 6000 francs per month.
Atkinson, 46, lives with his family in Zurich. Raised in the United Kingdom, he says that upon his arrival he booked an Airbnb on Langstrasse, when he had an infant: the choice placed him in the middle of a nightlife district. The episode explains why, in his view, without someone capable of guiding newcomers, people easily make wrong decisions. Switzerland remains attractive for its safety, nature, quality of life and environment for children, but relocation requires stronger motivations than mere earnings. ## The sector changes the value of the offer
The same professional offer does not carry the same weight for everyone. Atkinson distinguishes mainly between IT, finance and pharmaceuticals, and also links the assessment to the age of those relocating. The comparison therefore concerns not only the figure on the payslip, but the way work fits into everyday life.
| Profile | Element that attracts or puts off | | IT | Specialists ask for broad opportunities to work remotely; in Switzerland, being present in the office often remains the rule. | | Finance | More agile corporate structures than in London are an attraction. | | Pharmaceuticals | The Basel region is described as a natural draw. | | Younger people | The policy on free movement and the social climate carry weight. | | Older people | The choice focuses more on school and family. |
For those looking in annunci di lavoro, the first practical comparison is therefore between job duties and work organization. In the IT sector, recruitment from abroad becomes more difficult when specialists ask for broad opportunities to work remotely and office presence remains strong in Switzerland. Atkinson cites Germany, where salaries are lower but models are often more flexible. In finance, by contrast, the identified lever is the agility of corporate structures compared with London. For pharmaceuticals, the geographical reference is the Basel region.
The most unexpected difference may emerge as early as preschool. In the United Kingdom, Atkinson explains, nursery school focuses on academic learning from the outset. In a Swiss preschool, his son told him that he had learned to light matches and fend for himself in the woods: it was a shock for his father.
Behind the episode lies a different educational philosophy. The model described by Atkinson promotes autonomy and individual responsibility; academic achievement, in his experience, evens out later. His children grew up happy, healthy and extremely independent. For an international family, the question to ask is not only what salary to expect, but what view of childhood and schooling one will encounter after the move.
Language, too, should be considered without making assumptions. The Swiss approach to languages is open and, in many international companies, English is more than sufficient. This can facilitate entry into professional life, but it does not eliminate the other obstacles to integration mentioned in the interview. The choice therefore depends on the combination of work, age and family, not on a single ranking of attractiveness.

The decision can be turned into an orderly assessment, without treating salary as the only variable. The criteria that emerged from the interview help prepare a choice less exposed to errors.
### Four practical steps
1. Clarify the motivation. Before responding to an offer, write down what you are looking for beyond money: security, contact with nature, quality of life and an environment favorable to children. If salary is the only reason for the change, the interview suggests considering this motivation a warning sign.
2. Calculate the real margin. Set net salary alongside the first expenses cited by Atkinson: rent and cassa malati. The comparison must concern what remains for savings, investments or retirement, not the isolated salary figure. The assessment also serves to measure the difference compared with the situation in the United Kingdom, given as a point of comparison in the interview.
3. Prepare the home search. Define the family's needs immediately, including space for a home office, and do not choose an address without understanding its surroundings. The Airbnb experience on Langstrasse shows the risk of a decision made without guidance. Since many expats change accommodation several times in the first few months, the housing search should be treated as part of the professional decision.
4. Check work and school together. Ask how much office presence the role requires and how compatible the arrangement is with family needs. Then compare expectations regarding early childhood education: the Swiss system described by Atkinson prioritizes independence and responsibility, while the British experience starts with a more academic focus. The question is not which model is better, but which one is suitable for the children.
If one assessment remains open, it is advisable to pause the comparison and formulate a precise question for the company or the family: the transfer must hold up together in terms of work, housing and educational expectations. ## TL;DR - 988'700 tonnes of cement in the third quarter - Supplies up 1% compared with the same period - More than 98% of the volume is low-clinker - 32% by rail, 68% by road
## Key facts - Quantities in the third quarter → 988'700 tonnes - Change from the same period last year → 1% - First nine months → 2,8 million tonnes - Low-clinker cement → over 98% - Portland cement → 1% - Rail transport → 32% - Road transport → 68% - Industry association → Cemsuisse
988'700 tonnes of cement were delivered in Switzerland in the third quarter, 1% more than in the same period last year. The news was reported by Keystone-ATS and reflects a slight increase in the flow of supplies.
### Moderate growth, with demand still present
Over the first nine months, growth stood at a similar 1%, for a total of 2,8 million tonnes. The quarterly and cumulative figures therefore describe the same trend: quantities delivered increased, without the source reporting a larger change.
Cemsuisse, the industry association, writes in a statement that “Swiss quality cement continues to be in high demand.” On the path toward the goal of net-zero emissions, the association adds, the sector shows a strong propensity for innovation and makes significant investments to reduce the CO2 released by its products.
In recent years, demand for more environmentally friendly types of cement has continued to grow. Today, low-clinker types account for over 98% of the total volume delivered. Portland cement, used exclusively until the 1990s, represents only a marginal 1% share.
Cemsuisse presents the composition of supplies as a dual result: the sector makes an important contribution to the domestic supply of cement and concrete and supports the Confederation’s climate policy objectives.
From a logistics perspective, the tables published by the organization founded in 1881 indicate that 32% of deliveries in the January–September period took place by rail, compared with 68% by road. The rail share also fell by more than two percentage points in the comparison reported. Cemsuisse links this figure to problems with single-wagonload transport, which force companies to resort to trucks. Director Stefan Vannoni expresses the sector’s regret, while the organization reports that it has already repeatedly flagged the shortcomings of rail freight transport to the competent authorities. ## What the data indicate for the Swiss system
### Volume, product and transport are three different dimensions
To read the press release without confusing the levels, it is helpful to separate the quantity delivered, the type of cement and the means used to distribute it. These are three indicators present in the same picture, but they describe different aspects of the industry's activity.
The first figure concerns volumes. The increase is described as slight and concerns the third quarter; the cumulative figure for the first nine months follows the same 1% change. For a Swiss reader, this signals that demand remains active during the period under consideration. The scope of observation is cement supplies.
The second figure concerns the composition. The clear predominance of cements with a low clinker content, exceeding 98%, and the marginal presence of 1% Portland show what type of product makes up the delivered volume. Cemsuisse links this development to demand for more environmentally friendly solutions, innovation and investments to reduce CO2 emissions. The connection with the Confederation's climate policy is explicit in the press release, not an interpretation added from outside.
The third dimension is logistics. With 68% of supplies by road and 32% by rail, road transport was the prevailing channel in the January-September period. The explanation provided by the sector concerns the difficult conditions of single-wagon transport: companies are forced to use trucks. The problem identified is not attributed to the quality of the cement or to demand, but to the organization of freight transport by rail.
For those following the national economy, the operational point is therefore to distinguish an indicator of domestic supply from a logistics indicator. Cemsuisse maintains that the industry contributes to the domestic availability of cement and concrete and to climate targets. Those who want to set this reading alongside other economic topics can consult the guide to costo della vita in Svizzera, without confusing the supply-chain figure with a change in household costs.

### A five-step reading
To turn the press release into useful information, the reader can follow a sequence based on the categories used in the source.
1. Start with the period. Separate the third quarter from the total for the first nine months and do not overlap the two scopes. The first is used to read the quarterly trend; the second captures the cumulative figure indicated by Cemsuisse.
2. Establish the measure. Record the quantity in tonnes and the percentage change associated with each period. This keeps the increase in supplies linked to the correct figure and prevents it from being confused with the transport share or the composition of the cement.
3. Check the product. Look for the distinction between types with a low clinker content and Portland cement. This separation makes it possible to assess demand for materials described as more environmentally friendly, without attributing the same meaning to all types of cement.
4. Verify the logistics. Put rail and road in separate columns and read together the passage on the conditions of single-wagon transport. The source indicates that these conditions are precisely what drive companies to use trucks. To orient yourself regarding mobility services available in Switzerland, you can consult section mezzi pubblici.
5. Follow the stated responsibility. The press release is from Cemsuisse; the statements reported are attributed to director Stefan Vannoni; the shortcomings of rail freight transport have been reported to the competent authorities. This attribution keeps the organization’s point of view separate from the reference to the Confederation’s objectives.
The same framework helps track any updates without introducing extraneous data: volume, period, composition and delivery method remain separate. The reference to climate-policy objectives should also be read as the association’s position and argument, while the data on supplies describes the quantities reported in the press release.

## TL;DR - Kraken adds Frankencoin (ZCHF) to trading - The stablecoin is pegged to the Swiss franc - The announcement comes from an association based in Zug - Frankencoin has existed since 2023 and is backed by deposited assets
## Key facts - What → Frankencoin (ZCHF) - Platform → Kraken - Announcement → Frankencoin Association - Headquarters → Zug - Category → stablecoin - Peg → Swiss franc - Existence → since 2023 - Collateral → deposited assets held as backing
## The listing announced by Kraken
Kraken, an American cryptocurrency exchange, made Frankencoin (ZCHF) available for trading today. Frankencoin Association, a nonprofit organization headquartered in Zug, announced the news. For investors, this simplifies access to the cryptocurrency pegged to the Swiss franc.
The listing thus makes a stablecoin referenced to the Swiss franc available on the platform mentioned. Frankencoin falls into the stablecoin category, meaning digital currencies whose value is supposed to remain as stable as possible. Its reference is not the US dollar, as is the case with most stablecoins, but the Swiss franc. This is the feature that distinguishes the project within the landscape described by the source.
According to its promoters, Frankencoin is Switzerland's largest and most widespread stablecoin. The digital currency has existed since 2023 and is backed by assets deposited as collateral. The source therefore presents two elements together: an asset designed to keep its value stable and a collateral system supporting the coin.
### Issuance without a central authority
Users can generate new Frankencoin by providing adequate collateral, in the absence of a central authority responsible for issuance. The source links the listing to access to the platform's trading offering and describes the protocol's operation separately.
The association's role is also defined separately. Frankencoin Association serves as a point of contact, promotes development and supports the ecosystem, without controlling the protocol. This clarification helps interpret the announcement correctly: the American platform expands the access channel, while the association announces the news and performs support functions.
For the Swiss public, the geographic and economic references remain clear: the pegged currency is the franc, and the organization that disseminated the announcement is headquartered in Zug. Those who want to separate the issue of exchange rates from that of crypto can use comparatore CHF/EUR, as a tool distinct from the trading platform. ## What changes for those considering Frankencoin
The practical effect stated by the source is access. With its inclusion in Kraken's offering, investors find the crypto pegged to the franc on an American cryptocurrency exchange that includes it in trading. The development therefore concerns access to the trading channel, while the peg, the backing and the protocol are the elements to read in the description of the coin.
### Three questions for reading the development
The first question concerns the unit of reference. Frankencoin uses the Swiss franc, whereas most of the stablecoins mentioned by the source are pegged to the US dollar. For a reader who thinks in CHF, the difference is immediate: the project presents itself as a crypto linked to the Swiss franc, not as a dollar-based stablecoin.
The second concerns stability. The definition of stablecoin refers to a value that should remain as stable as possible. That conditional must be retained when reading the project: the source describes the category's objective, it does not present an absolute promise of unchanging value. The peg to the franc and the stability pursued are connected, but they are not the same information.
The third concerns backing. Frankencoin is backed by deposited assets; in addition, users can create new Frankencoin by depositing adequate collateral. The source does not attribute this function to a central issuer. Separating backing, creation and access on the platform avoids confusing three different aspects. Therefore, accessibility and issuance do not coincide: the first term concerns presence on the exchange, the second the users' collateral and the absence of a central authority.
| Reading point | Available information | |---|---| | Reference currency | Swiss franc | | Category | Stablecoin | | Backing | Deposited assets | | Creation | Users with adequate collateral | | Central authority | There is no central issuing authority |
### The boundary between association and protocol
To interpret the project, it is equally useful to distinguish the role of the Frankencoin Association. The nonprofit organization is a point of contact, promotes development and supports the ecosystem. The source specifies, however, that it does not control the protocol. For an exchange-rate comparison, comparatore CHF/EUR should be kept separate from the description of Frankencoin: it helps with the exchange rate, it does not replace the source's information about the digital coin.

The news can be read without confusing its presence on Kraken with the structure of the project. The first step is to identify the asset precisely: the name is Frankencoin and the code indicated is ZCHF. This avoids stopping at the sole word stablecoin and losing the reference to the Swiss franc.
Second: verify the currency to which it is pegged. The source clearly distinguishes Frankencoin from most stablecoins pegged to the American dollar. The comparison must therefore be made based on the monetary reference, not merely on the fact that it is a digital currency.
Third: read the wording about stability for what it says. The value should remain as stable as possible. The wording describes a category objective and must not be transformed into a certainty different from the one reported.
Fourth: consider the backing and creation. Frankencoin has existed since 2023 and is backed by deposited assets serving as collateral. Users can create new Frankencoins when they deposit adequate collateral. These are two pieces of information to keep together to understand the mechanism described.
Fifth: separate the roles. Frankencoin Association, based in Zug, is nonprofit; it serves as a point of reference for contacts, promotes development and supports the ecosystem. However, it does not control the protocol. Kraken, on the other hand, is the American cryptocurrency exchange that adds ZCHF to its trading offering.
### What the guide allows you to verify
This sequence makes it possible to distinguish access, pegging, collateral and roles without attributing effects to the announcement that the source does not indicate. If the interest is access, the data to check is the inclusion in Kraken's offering. If the interest is how it works, the relevant points are the deposited assets, users' collateral and the absence of a central authority. If the interest is the entity supporting the project, the reference is the association in Zug, with the explicit limitation that it does not control the protocol.

## TL;DR - Swisscom prices unchanged until the end of September 2028 - Two-year extension of tariff caps - Maximum of 24 francs per month, excluding VAT - No increase for one-off charges
## Key facts - Expiry: end of September 2028 - Extension: two years - Maximum: 24 francs per month, excluding VAT - Operators: Sunrise, Salt and Init7 - One-off charges: no increase
Until the end of September 2028, Swisscom will keep unchanged the prices it charges other telecommunications operators for use of the fiber-optic network. The extension was agreed with Price Surveillance and extends the tariff limits already in force by two years.
The previous regulation was due to expire at the end of the month. Before extending the agreement, Mister Prezzi analyzed updated information provided by Swisscom on the costs and revenues of the fiber-optic network. The outcome was announced today in a newsletter issued by Stefan Meierhans's office.
### What remains unchanged
For Swisscom's competitors, including Sunrise, Salt and Init7, the financial benchmark remains unchanged: they will continue to pay what they have paid to date, with a maximum of 24 francs per month, excluding VAT. This figure concerns the price Swisscom charges other operators for use of the fiber-optic network.
The confirmation also covers one-off charges. The federal office told the Awp news agency that no other prices of this type will be increased, including the fee for a new activation.
The agreement thus extends the existing arrangement without changing the monthly cap and without adjusting the one-off charges listed in the communication. The decision stems from the updated data examined by Mister Prezzi, not from a new amount announced for the service.
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the distinction to keep in mind is the nature of the price: the source refers to the sums paid by competitors to Swisscom, not to an amount presented as a direct tariff for the end customer. The time frame indicated is precise: the current conditions remain in force until the end of September 2028.
The shift from the end-of-month expiry to the new 2028 deadline is at the heart of the decision. The communication contains no new cap: the limits already applied are being extended, along with confirmation that the one-off charges will not increase. ## The before-and-after comparison
The practical result of the extension is the continuity of the framework for operators that use Swisscom's fiber-optic network. The difference compared with the previous situation is not a new amount, but the continuation of the agreement beyond the expiry that had been scheduled for the end of the month. The period indicated extends the current caps until the end of September 2028.

item.title: AI and semiconductors drive trade, WTO revises growth
item.description: Semiconduttori e server: commercio in crescita del 67%
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Semiconductors and servers: trade up 67% - AI fueled 47% of global growth - WTO estimate: from 1,9% to 3,9% for the year - World trade forecast to grow 4,1% in 2027
## Key facts - AI-related goods → semiconductors and servers - Trade in these goods → 67% compared with the same period in 2025 - Share of global growth → 47% - WTO forecast → from 1,9% to 3,9% - First six months of 2026 → merchandise trade grew by 3,5% - Energy → oil -24%; liquefied natural gas -47%; global decline of 6% and 1% - AI investment in 2027 → growth of at least 30% - 2027 forecasts → trade 4,1%; GDP 2,6% this year and 2,9% next year
## WTO updates the forecast
Trade in artificial intelligence-related goods recorded a 67% increase this year compared with the corresponding period in 2025. Semiconductors and servers contributed 47% of the expansion of the global market, prompting the World Trade Organization (WTO), based in Geneva, to raise its annual growth forecast from 1,9% to 3,9%.
Director-General Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala outlined the revision in a note released on Thursday. She acknowledged the multilateral trading system's ability to adapt to turbulence, while warning that the shock had hit some countries harder than others.
### From the trade surprise to energy
Merchandise trade grew by 3,5% in the first six months of 2026, exceeding expectations set in March. Chief economist Robert Staiger attributed the figure to the resilience of trade despite the war in the Middle East.
> “We were surprised that the war in the Middle East did not reduce global trade as much as we thought,” said chief economist Robert Staiger.
The energy trend was different: exports of crude oil from the Middle East fell by 24%, while those of liquefied natural gas declined by 47%. Thanks to increased supplies from other regions, the global decline remained at 6% and 1%, respectively.
The main driver remains artificial intelligence. Staiger said that the increase in trade in semiconductors and servers was greater than expected: a figure below 30% had been expected. For 2027, investment in AI infrastructure is expected to grow by at least 30%. Okonjo-Iweala nevertheless deplored the fact that access to these technologies is not equal for all states.
Regional prospects diverge: Asian exports are expected to post the largest increase, at 9,9%, ahead of those from the northern part of the American continent and Africa. Europe is expected to see a decline of 0,1%, while the Middle East could suffer a contraction of almost 18%. ## From the global forecast to a Swiss perspective
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the explicit connection in the news is the WTO's Geneva headquarters. However, the source does not provide a figure for Switzerland: it discusses the global market, energy supplies from the Middle East, exporting regions and GDP prospects. The figure must therefore be read as an international indicator, not as an automatic change in salary, the cost of living or employment in the country.
### Three distinctions to keep in mind
The first concerns timing. The 3,5% describes the first six months of 2026; the 4,1% is a WTO forecast for world trade in 2027. The revision from 1,9% to 3,9%, on the other hand, concerns the estimate for the year. Putting these values on the same footing would produce an incorrect comparison between an already recorded figure and a forecast.
The second concerns the subject. The 67% measures the increase in trade in AI-related goods, while the 47% indicates how much that dynamic fueled growth in the global market. The 3,5% concerns trade in goods as a whole. These are related indicators, but not interchangeable.
| Interpretation | Source data | Limitation for the Swiss public | |---|---|---| | Time horizon | 3,5% in the first six months of 2026 | not a Swiss figure | | Forecast | 4,1% growth in world trade in 2027 | not a forecast for the cantons | | Regions | Asia 9,9%; Europe contraction of 0,1%; Middle East nearly 18% decline | not a breakdown of Swiss exports |
The third concerns geography. Asia, Europe and the Middle East have different prospects; the source does not translate those figures into Swiss exports. It does not report a decision by the Federal Council or the cantons, nor data from SECO, UST/BFS or BNS/SNB. It does not announce changes to the cost of living. For this reason, the note does not allow an effect on taxes, incomes or daily expenses to be inferred.
For a personal check, comparison with costo della vita in Svizzera can be a separate step: it does not replace WTO data and does not derive from them a figure for a salary or a family.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to read and use the note
The most solid procedure for a Swiss reader is to separate the information into four steps, without turning a global forecast into a national announcement.
### Four practical steps
1. Set the period. Mark separately the comparison of AI-related trade with the same period in 2025, the first six months of 2026, and the forecasts for 2027. The note presents results and expectations: keeping them distinct prevents an assumption from being read as an already-acquired result.
2. Classify the indicator. Place AI-related goods, merchandise trade, energy, investment in AI infrastructure, regional exports, and GDP into different categories. Percentages referring to different things should neither be added nor compared without indicating what they refer to.
3. Check the geography. A value for the global market, a decline in the Middle East, or growth in Asia does not automatically describe Switzerland. The text mentions Geneva as the headquarters of the WTO, but does not provide a Swiss series to substitute for the global or regional data.
4. Separate source and decision. Attribute the revision to the WTO, the surprise at the resilience of trade to Robert Staiger, and the assessment of access to technologies to Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala. Statements relating to 2027 should be marked as forecasts.
After this verification, the general picture can be compared with one's own situation. busta paga svizzera helps read the income already indicated, while costo della vita in Svizzera offers a separate comparison; neither tool changes the WTO's percentages.
The final step is to relate the comparison to one's own income and taxes with calcolatore stipendio/imposte.
