item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Federal Supreme Court rejects an appeal by a divorced father. - Custody of the children alternates between the parents. - No deduction of 9'000 francs per child. - Maintenance payments already deducted rule out double tax relief.
## Key facts - Place: Canton Lucerne - Authority: Federal Supreme Court - Amount: 9'000 francs per child - Custody: alternating - Official residence of the children: with the mother - Outcome: appeal dismissed - Reason: double relief not provided for by law
## The ruling in the Lucerne case A divorced father residing in Canton Lucerne with several children cannot obtain a health insurance premium reduction based on the flat-rate deduction for children that the compensation office denied him. The Federal Supreme Court dismissed the appeal and deemed the cantonal decision lawful. The case directly concerns riduzione dei premi della cassa malati, but the decisive issue is the relationship between maintenance payments already deducted and a second deduction.
According to the judgment published today, the man and his ex-wife care for the children in alternating weeks. The divorce judgment awarded custody to both parents and established alternating custody. The children’s residence is nevertheless with the mother, where they are officially registered. Expenses incurred during each custody period are borne by the parent with whom the children are staying at that time. The father also pays the mother maintenance, which also serves to cover part of the costs of health insurance and healthcare.
The parent already benefits from the deduction for maintenance payments made to his ex-wife; allowing one for the children as well would have resulted in double relief, which is not provided for by law.
The cantonal court linked this interpretation to case law on tax deductions for dependent children. It referred to the Federal Direct Federal Tax Act, which excludes additional deductions when deductions for maintenance payments have already been claimed. It did not consider it decisive that the father cares for the children in rotation and bears the expenses during the custody periods.
For applications for premium reductions, the review takes place as part of mass administration, with standardized and automated processing of case files. The Federal Supreme Court therefore considered the cantonal conclusions compatible with higher-ranking law and dismissed the appeal. Moreover, cantonal law does not establish who is entitled to the flat-rate deduction in cases of alternating custody. ## The practical issue: a single tax allowance for the children The Lucerne decision compares four facts that can coexist in everyday life but did not carry the same weight in calculating the tax allowance. The father pays maintenance, has the children stay with him every other week, bears the expenses when they are with him and has the children officially registered with their mother. The cantonal court and the Federal Supreme Court, however, focused the calculation on the deduction already linked to the maintenance payments and on the civil domicile.
| Element | Reading in the case | |---|---| | Maintenance payments made to the mother | Already deducted by the father | | Alternating custody | Not enough to add the deduction | | Expenses during custody periods | Borne by the custodial parent | | Civil domicile | With the mother, operational reference |
The criterion followed by the judges can be understood as follows: the maintenance contribution paid to the mother already contributes to covering health insurance and healthcare expenses. Recognizing the 9'000 francs per child as well would have resulted in the disputed double tax relief. Expenses paid directly during alternating custody did not alter this conclusion.
### The grey area identified by the Federal Supreme Court The highest judicial authority nevertheless pointed out an inconsistency in the cantonal reasoning. For practical reasons, the Cantonal Court used the children's domicile as shown in the residents' register. That same decision-making process, however, ruled out in-depth checks of the custody arrangements, even though those arrangements were governed by the divorce judgment. In other words, the document was used to determine the domicile and maintenance obligations, while the actual custody arrangement was not examined in the same way.
This observation did not result in the appeal being allowed. The Federal Supreme Court indicated that other solutions are possible, but confirmed that Lucerne law does not specify who is entitled to the flat-rate deduction when custody is alternating. The judgment therefore does not automatically grant the benefit to the parent who bears the expenses during their weeks.
The parallel with dichiarazione delle imposte remains an element of the cantonal reasoning: the Federal Direct Tax Act was cited to support excluding an additional deduction when maintenance payments have already been deducted. For the case at hand, the practical point is to distinguish the right to custody from the possibility of combining two deductions.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to check your own case To examine a decision on the reduction of premiums in a situation of alternating custody, it is advisable to reconstruct the facts in the same order in which they emerge from the Lucerne case. The aim is not to automatically add up all expenses incurred, but to understand which item has already been used for the deduction and which domicile was taken into account.
### Four practical steps
1. Retrieve the divorce judgment. In the case examined, the appellant submitted it to the court. From that document, the previous instance obtained information on maintenance obligations and the children's domicile, as well as the custody arrangements.
2. Distinguish maintenance payments from custody expenses. The contribution paid to the mother must be kept separate from the costs incurred directly during the weeks in which the children are in the father's or the other parent's care. The decision considers the maintenance payments already deducted and does not turn custody expenses into a second deduction.
3. Verify the civil domicile. The children are officially registered with the mother, and this information was used as a reference in the standardized processing of the applications. The domicile recorded by the residents' registration office therefore had a concrete bearing on the case.
4. Compare the decision with cantonal law. In Lucerne, the flat-rate deduction is 9'000 francs per child, but the law does not determine who is entitled to it in cases of alternating custody. The review must therefore focus on the determining income, the maintenance payments already claimed, and the reasoning of the compensation office.
### If the decision is challenged In this case, the process went from the compensation office to the Lucerne Cantonal Court and finally to the Federal Supreme Court. The judgment does not indicate an automatic entitlement for the parent who shares the weeks with the former spouse. Instead, it shows that the appeal must address the precise reason for the refusal: avoiding double relief.
Before assessing a challenge, therefore, it is useful to assemble the divorce judgment, the calculation of the determining income, and the decision received. The costs incurred during custody alone do not determine the outcome of the case examined.

## TL;DR - Switzerland ranks first in the IMD World Talent Ranking - Adjusted EU/EFTA gap: 1,1% lower - Third countries: 4,5% lower - Immigration via free movement of persons: 77%
## Key facts - ILO data period → 2015-2020 - IMD World Talent Ranking → first place - Global Talent Competitiveness Index → second place - Immigrant nursing staff in high-income countries → 19,6% less than non-immigrant colleagues - Adjusted salary of EU/EFTA nationals in Switzerland → 1,1% lower than that of Swiss nationals - Adjusted salary of third-country nationals → 4,5% lower than that of Swiss nationals - Permanent immigration through free movement with the EU/EFTA → 77% - Average unexplained gap in high-income countries → about ten percentage points
## Switzerland's leading position Switzerland has ranked first in the IMD World Talent Ranking for years and is second in the Global Talent Competitiveness Index. The OECD also ranks it among the most attractive countries for highly skilled workers in its Indicators of Talent Attractiveness. The wage data adds a less well-known element: holding a foreign passport has almost no impact on salary.
An ILO report finds that in many highly developed economies, immigrants earn lower wages than residents even with the same qualifications. Once education, professional experience, age, sector and place of work are taken into account, an unexplained difference of about ten percentage points remains on average. Women are disproportionately affected, and in high-income countries, immigrant nursing staff receive, on average, pay 19,6% lower than their non-immigrant colleagues.
Switzerland is an exception, especially compared with Denmark, the Netherlands, Ireland and Sweden: for people from the EU/EFTA, the adjusted wage gap is virtually nonexistent.
### The comparison between the ILO and SECO ILO data cover the period 2015-2020. The organization clarifies that no more recent, comparable international calculations are available.
For Switzerland, a more recent analysis by SECO is available. After adjustment, the equivalent salary of people from EU/EFTA countries is 1,1% lower, within the margin of statistical uncertainty. SECO writes:
> «The data suggest that, in general, people who arrived through free movement seek pay similar to that of Swiss citizens and are able to obtain it».
For nationals of third countries, the difference rises to 4,5%. SECO links it primarily to structural factors: qualifications obtained outside the EU/EFTA are not always comparable or valued in the same way, while language proficiency could play a role.
The source does not attribute the result to a special law against discrimination based on origin or nationality. The equal-treatment law in fact protects only against discrimination based on gender. The explanation given is the composition of immigration: about 77% of permanent immigration over the past 15 years came through free movement with the EU/EFTA. Many of those who arrived have a high level of education, comparable qualifications, speak a national language or work for international companies where English is the main language. For those considering new opportunities, the first point of comparison nevertheless remains in annunci di lavoro. ## From statistics to choosing a job The Swiss figure does not describe a rule that assigns the same salary to everyone arriving from abroad. Instead, it describes a market in which, after adjusting for education, work experience, age, sector and place of work, the gap between Swiss and immigrant workers becomes very small for the EU/EFTA group. The distinction from third countries is therefore necessary to interpret the figures correctly.
| Group | Adjusted result | Reading indicated by the source | |---|---|---| | EU/EFTA | 1,1% lower, within the margin of uncertainty | Requirements and salaries similar to those in Switzerland | | Third countries | 4,5% lower | Structural factors, qualifications and language |
### The correct comparison For a female or male worker, the practical consequence is not to use their passport as the sole parameter. The soundest comparison starts with the variables considered by the analysis: education, experience, age, sector and place of work. If these characteristics are comparable, the Swiss result indicates a very small disparity for people from the EU/EFTA. The same interpretation cannot automatically be applied to people from third countries, for whom the source describes a larger difference linked mainly to structural factors.
Here, the structure of immigration is decisive. Over the last 15 years, the free movement of persons with the EU/EFTA has accounted for about 77% of permanent immigration. According to the source, many of these people have a high level of education and qualifications that are relatively comparable in the Swiss labor market. Some already know a national language; others are employed by international companies where English is the main language. These factors help explain how talent attractiveness and a small wage gap can coexist.
The Swiss average may also be influenced by the salaries of highly specialized professionals and executives, which raise the overall figure. This does not erase the differences between individual profiles, but explains why the national figure should not be read as an individual promise.
Two levels remain that should not be confused. The ILO allows international comparison for the 2015-2020 period, while SECO offers a more recent analysis for Switzerland; however, the international organization points out the absence of new and comparable calculations. To move from the statistical average to your own salary document, you can consult the guide to busta paga svizzera.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to turn statistics into a comparison The source does not present an administrative procedure, a deadline, or a document to use to obtain a salary that is aligned. The concrete action for those who work or are looking for work in Switzerland is to build a comparison that does not conflate groups, periods, and qualifications. The following approach stays within the available data.
### Four steps 1. **Identify the comparison group.** Before interpreting a pay difference, distinguish people from the EU/EFTA from those from third countries. The source shows that the two results are not interchangeable; using a single average would erase precisely the distinction considered by SECO.
2. Separate observed salary and adjusted salary. Note whether the comparison takes education, professional experience, age, sector, and place of work into account. These are the factors indicated in the source: without this check, a raw difference does not show whether the passport actually had an impact.
3. Check qualifications and language. For qualifications obtained outside the EU/EFTA, comparability and recognition on the Swiss labor market are not always equivalent. Language proficiency could play a role. If the activity takes place in an international company, the reference to English as the main working language, an element mentioned by the source, must also be considered.
4. Separate the periods. Use the ILO data for 2015-2020 for the international comparison and the SECO data for the more up-to-date Swiss analysis, without presenting them as if they were the same series. The ILO notes that it does not have more recent calculations that are internationally comparable.
### What the reader can conclude The result of the verification should remain proportionate. International statistics describe an average gap; the Swiss analysis measures differences after adjustment. Neither data point alone offers a promise about every person’s salary. Instead, they offer a criterion for assessing an offer: ask whether the profile is comparable, which statistical group is relevant, and which period is being used.
This reading can support both the search for a job and the review of a proposal already received. It is advisable to keep the data on education, experience, sector, and place of work separate, because these are precisely the variables used to adjust the comparison. In this way, the reader avoids automatically attributing to nationality a difference that the source also links to qualifications or language.
To translate this verification into a comparison of your own income, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: Switzerland leads in robotics: 217 companies and 7'000 jobs
item.description: 217 aziende nella robotica svizzera
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 217 companies in Swiss robotics - 109 directly produce robots - 87% have fewer than 100 employees - Approximately 7’000 jobs in the sector
## Key facts - Companies in the sector → 217 - Direct manufacturers → 109 - Spin-offs from ETH and EPFL → approximately 80% - Companies with fewer than 100 employees → 87% - Jobs → approximately 7’000
### A snapshot of the sector
217 Swiss companies are linked to the robotics sector, and 109 of these directly design and manufacture robots. The latest economic monitoring report published by Raiffeisen describes a rapidly growing ecosystem closely linked to university research. Drones, underwater robots, and medical and industrial applications are all part of the same snapshot.
In July 2026, in Geneva, humanoid robots from Geneva-based company RB Labs were among the audience at an AI summit. The episode belongs to the public dimension of the sector, while Raiffeisen’s data mainly measure companies, spin-offs and employment.
### From research to companies
More than half of the companies originate from Swiss universities and research institutes. The Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich (ETH) and the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Lausanne (EPFL) play a central role: approximately 80% of university spin-offs active in robotics originate from the two institutions. This share directly links academic research to the creation of new business ventures.
### Drones, snakes and seabeds
Researchers at the University of Zurich aim to use unmanned systems to inspect pylons, bridges and cargo ships. The technologies can also be used in fires and to search for survivors. Roboa, a company founded at ETH Zurich, develops snake-shaped robots to inspect pipes and hard-to-access spaces. Tethys Robotics develops underwater robots to monitor offshore infrastructure and carry out other operations in marine environments.
The majority of companies in the sector are small in size: 87% employ fewer than 100 employees. Approximately 7’000 people are employed in the sector overall. This structure shows that Swiss robotics also includes specialized companies born from research, in addition to industrial applications.
In terms of financing, Switzerland stands out in the European landscape. The European Spinouts Report 2025 puts the venture capital raised by robotics spin-offs originating at ETH at approximately 785 million dollars, and the amount flowing into ventures linked to EPFL at approximately 508 million. Anyone observing the labor market can use annunci di lavoro nella robotica to verify how this research translates into concrete positions. ## Impact on employment and the economy
### An already high industrial density
The figure that speaks most clearly to those working in factories is density: in Switzerland, there are 29 industrial robots for every thousand employees in the manufacturing sector. The figure is higher than that recorded in France, Austria, Canada and China. The comparison shows that automation is already measurable in Swiss factories, not only in experimental projects.
### The tasks most exposed
According to the estimates contained in Raiffeisen's report, robotics could affect approximately one in three jobs in Switzerland in the future. To interpret the figure in practical terms, it is necessary to consider the activities performed, not only the sector indicated in the contract.
| Area | What the analysis indicates | |---|---| | Industry and construction | Greater potential for robotization | | Technical and operational tasks | Exposure for auxiliary roles, electricians, operators and metalworkers | | Assistance, care and support | More gradual adoption because of the high level of human contact |
The flow of capital confirms the variety of applications. Investments concern minimally invasive surgery and agriculture, including autonomous systems for weed control. In tests in Aargau, the robot trained with artificial intelligence eliminated 90% of weeds on the second pass. Robotics is therefore entering activities beyond manufacturing, with uneven effects on jobs.
### The labor shortage remains a separate problem
The report puts a limit on the idea that robots can automatically make up for the shortage of skilled labor. Among occupations characterized by a particular shortage of workers, only 17% also show above-average exposure to robotics. In activities involving extensive human contact, such as assistance, care and support for people, adoption is expected to be more gradual. According to the analysis, human skills will remain difficult to replace at least in the medium term.
For those seeking opportunities, the catalog of aziende che assumono allows one to move from the general figure to the employers to examine, without mistaking a profession's exposure for an individual forecast.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to use this data for guidance
The growth of the sector provides an indication, not a ready-made choice. Anyone living or working in Switzerland can turn the data into a structured professional assessment, without assigning the same level of exposure to robotics to every role. The following procedure helps prepare an application or assess a possible move into an activity connected to the sector.
### An operational sequence
1. **Map your current job.** Write down the tasks you perform and compare them with the categories indicated in the study: support staff, electricians, machinery and plant operators, metalworking workers. If the job involves assistance, care or accompaniment, note the high level of human contact, associated with more gradual adoption.
2. Choose an area of interest. The source indicates applications in drones, mobile and underwater robots, minimally invasive surgery, industry and agriculture. Identifying a specific field helps you read job advertisements without treating robotics as a single occupation.
3. Check the company profile. The monitoring distinguishes the 109 companies that design and directly produce robots from the total of 217 companies linked to the sector. Before applying, check what activity the company describes and whether it is consistent with the area chosen.
4. Compare the role and opportunities. Examine the responsibilities required, the interaction with machinery or autonomous systems, and the level of human contact. Set yourself a personal deadline to complete this assessment before submitting the application, then update the evaluation for each new position.
A one-page grid can contain four items: current activity, application area, exposure indicated by the study, and required human skills. This framework prevents reading the overall number of jobs as a guarantee for every profession. The report in fact notes that many human skills will remain difficult to replace at least in the medium term.
To compare current income with a new opportunity, the final step is to use the calcolatore stipendio.

## TL;DR - Raiffeisen raises its 2026 GDP estimate to 1,7% - For 2027, it confirms growth of 1,3% - 2026 inflation at 0,7%, versus the previously estimated 0,5% - The SNB could raise interest rates on 10 December
## Key facts - Location → St. Gallen - Institution → Raiffeisen - GDP 2026 → 1,7%, excluding the effects of major sporting events - Previous 2026 GDP estimate → 0,8% - GDP 2027 → 1,3% - Inflation 2026 → 0,7%, versus the previous 0,5% - Inflation 2027 → 1,1%, versus the previous 0,8% - Next SNB review → December 10
ST. GALLEN – Raiffeisen economists have significantly revised upward their forecasts for the Swiss economy and expect the Swiss National Bank (SNB) to soon end its zero-interest-rate policy.
In an analysis published today, the cooperative estimates that in 2026 gross domestic product (GDP), excluding the effects of major sporting events, will increase by 1,7%, compared with the 0,8% previously forecast. For 2027, however, Raiffeisen maintains its forecast of growth of 1,3%.
### The signals behind the revision
In the institution's view, the Swiss economy continues to recover and, so far, has been little affected by the war in the Middle East. Even the latest escalation of the conflict in September did not dent business confidence.
The picture was supported above all by second-quarter growth data, which came in stronger than expected thanks to the dynamism of the pharmaceutical sector. The upward revision therefore follows economic indicators considered more solid than previously expected.
Raiffeisen has also revised its inflation forecasts upward. For 2026, it forecasts a price increase of 0,7%, compared with the 0,5% previously indicated. For 2027, the expectation is 1,1%, compared with the previous 0,8%.
Specialists explain that the impact of high energy prices should last longer than hoped. Core inflation, on the other hand, is expected to rise as a result of the franc's weakening and greater pressure from abroad.
Hence the possibility that the SNB could raise rates as early as its next assessment of the economic and monetary situation, scheduled for December 10. Raiffeisen notes that the economy is operating close to its potential and that inflation remains within the bank's target range, between 0 and 2%. According to its analysts, keeping rates at zero, so far a measure supporting the economy, is therefore becoming less and less appropriate. The institution is headed by Martin Schlegel. The Raiffeisen report offers two perspectives for those who live or work in Switzerland. On the one hand, expected growth for 2026 is revised sharply upward. On the other, the price trajectory is also revised upward. costo della vita in Svizzera is therefore the practical topic to monitor alongside economic conditions.
### The twofold signal for the reader
The figures do not describe the same thing and should not be considered on the same footing. GDP measures the pace of economic growth, while inflation estimates show how Raiffeisen sees price developments. Comparing the previous and new forecasts makes the change in scenario visible:
| Indicator | Previous estimate | New indication | |---|---:|---:| | GDP 2026 | 0,8% | 1,7% | | GDP 2027 | — | 1,3%, confirmed | | Inflation 2026 | 0,5% | 0,7% | | Inflation 2027 | 0,8% | 1,1% |
The practical takeaway is that the bank sees more momentum in growth, but also more persistent price increases than previously estimated. The source links this second revision to the persistence of high energy prices, the weaker franc and pressure from abroad. It is therefore not a single indicator, but two developments to monitor separately.
For the SNB, the point of intersection is the target range between 0 and 2%. Raiffeisen's projected inflation remains within it, while the economy moves closer to its potential. Analysts base the prospect of a forthcoming rate hike on this combination. This does not mean, however, that the decision has already been made: the report speaks of the possibility of action at the next review on 10 December.
The weaker franc is one of the factors cited for underlying price increases. Those who want to keep this factor separate from price developments can read the report alongside a comparatore CHF/EUR. What should not be anticipated remains the SNB's decision: until the review mentioned, this is a Raiffeisen forecast and not the announcement of a measure already adopted.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. To follow any potential shift in the direction of monetary policy without confusing forecasts and decisions, it is advisable to create a simple monitoring sheet. The source already provides all the necessary elements: reference years, previous estimates, new guidance, causes of rising prices and the date of the SNB review.
### A four-step procedure
1. **Separate the indicators.** Create two separate rows: one for GDP growth and one for inflation. Do not mix the gross domestic product figure with the one for the increase in prices.
2. Place the before and after side by side. For 2026, record the change from 0,8% to 1,7% for GDP and from 0,5% to 0,7% for inflation. For 2027, note the confirmed growth of 1,3% and the expected price increase of 1,1%, compared with the previous 0,8%.
3. Mark December 10. This is the date of the next review of the economic and monetary situation. It should be treated as a date to watch: Raiffeisen indicates that the SNB could intervene, not that a rate hike has already been decided.
4. Check the reasons. In the next update, verify whether energy prices, the weaker franc and pressure from abroad remain central. These are the factors Raiffeisen links to the development of underlying inflation.
This sequence makes it possible to read any updates without turning a forecast into a certainty. It also helps distinguish what concerns growth from what concerns prices, while keeping the reference to the target range between 0 and 2%.

## TL;DR
- Nearly 5'000 AI job postings between July 2025 and June 2026 - Demand for AI is growing by 32% in one year - The public sector records the largest increase: 67% - Zurich accounts for 45% of Swiss postings
## Key facts
- Period → July 2025-June 2026 - AI job postings → nearly 5'000 - Annual growth → 32% - Main sector → IT, 1'211 offers - Public institutions → 67% more listings - SMEs → 76% of the increase and 62% of positions - Zurich → 2'181 listings, 45% of the national total - Study sample → 8'439 postings
Between July 2025 and June 2026, nearly 5'000 job postings related to artificial intelligence were published in Switzerland. Compared with the previous twelve months, the number increased by 32%. This figure is at the heart of the Swiss AI Jobs Report 2026 by Hochschule Lucerne.
The study provides a snapshot of a market that is not limited to the technology sector. Demand rose in all ten main areas of activity considered: these include, in addition to information technology and finance and insurance, education and research, the chemical-pharmaceutical, commercial and logistics sectors, the public sector, engineering and industry, as well as legal and business consulting and healthcare.
In absolute terms, IT remains ahead with 1'211 offers. The sharpest change, however, comes from public institutions, which increased listings by 67%. According to the study's author, Curdin Derungs, this growth indicates that politics and public administration are strengthening their confidence in AI as the technology of the future.
The expansion is driven by small and medium-sized enterprises, responsible for 76% of the recorded increase and 62% of all published positions. The report describes AI as a presence entering the processes and services of established SMEs, no longer limited to major technology groups.
### From quantity to profiles
Positions in Data Engineering and Machine Learning Engineering account for nearly 40% of postings: these are profiles that build data infrastructure and ensure the functioning of AI models. Demand is also growing for Product Owners, Managers and AI Consultants, who are tasked with identifying business applications and guiding their implementation.
Recruitment focuses on candidates with experience and a combination of technical and strategic skills. Senior positions increased by 42%. Opportunities remain for people at the beginning of their careers, but permanent junior positions represent only 5% of the total.
Derungs points out that the market is described as extremely selective by those seeking their first job and that the search is challenging even for candidates with years of experience.
The report thus provides a useful framework for navigating among the annunci di lavoro, distinguishing the type of role from the simple AI label. ## What changes in how the market is read
The +32% does not merely describe a quantitative increase. The report's map shows that AI appears across different activities: data, product management, consulting, finance, healthcare, industry and administration. For job seekers, this broadens the possible entry points, but makes a search built around a single job title less effective.
### Profiles that do not overlap
The report compares two families of roles that address different needs. Data Engineering and Machine Learning Engineering work on data infrastructure and model operations. Product Owner, Manager and AI Consultant, on the other hand, are associated with identifying business applications and implementing them. For the reader, this distinction helps clarify whether a position mainly involves technical construction or connecting technology with business applications.
The role of SMEs adds another practical element. Growth is not concentrated solely in large technology groups: the report attributes the largest share of the increase and a significant share of the published positions to SMEs. Those who want to turn this data into a concrete search can include aziende che assumono alongside large companies, including established SMEs, without limiting the search to the best-known names.
### An uneven geography
The market does not show the same intensity in every area. Canton Zurich accounts for 2'181 postings, equivalent to 45% of the national total. In the cantons of Central Switzerland, the report indicates between 100 and 140 listings per 100'000 inhabitants, compared with a Swiss average of 96. In Canton Lucerne, postings grew by 55%.
| Area | Data | Interpretation | |---|---|---| | Canton Zurich | 2'181 postings; 45% of the total | greatest concentration | | Central Switzerland | 100-140 listings per 100'000 inhabitants; average 96 | above average | | Canton Lucerne | growth of 55% | increase in postings |
These data suggest a search broken down by area: the Zurich pool remains the largest, while Central Switzerland shows a higher-than-average density of listings. The national figure alone does not describe the differences between the cantons. Separating region, sector and role type makes it possible to read the demand captured by the report more precisely.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to use the report for guidance
To use the report as a guide, separate three questions: what type of role to look for, which sectors to explore and which areas to focus the search on. The figures do not indicate a single AI profession; they show different skill families and territories. From there, a straightforward path can be built.
### Four practical steps
1. Define the profile. If you are looking for a technical role, look at positions related to Data Engineering or Machine Learning Engineering; if you are interested in the connection with the business, consider Product Owner, Manager and AI Consultant.
2. Broaden the sectors. Don't stop at IT: the analysis also includes finance and insurance, education and research, the chemical-pharmaceutical, commercial and logistics sectors, the public sector, engineering and industry, as well as legal and business consulting and healthcare.
3. Rank the areas. Compare Canton Zurich, Central Switzerland and Canton Lucerne using the period and number of job postings indicated by the report.
4. Read seniority levels cautiously. The growth in senior positions does not automatically make the search easy: the report points to difficulties even for experienced profiles, while permanent junior jobs remain a small share.

The distinction matters because Swiss areas of responsibility are not interchangeable. The President of the Swiss Confederation, Guy Parmelin, announced his resignation from the Federal Council, effective December 31, 2026; Parliament will elect his successor at its next session.
### The announcement and the federal calendar
The announcement places the president's departure on a precise date and identifies Parliament as the next step. The Swiss Government's page brings together the announcement with other federal dossiers, each with a different timeframe.
Starting in January, the adjustment of OASI/DI pensions will take account of price and wage developments. The expected increase is around 1,6%. The maximum permitted contribution to the third pillar will also increase in the same update. The portal thus presents a change linked to pension provision and price and wage developments.
The financial section concerns Switzerland's international role. The Government believes that the country should be able to continue contributing to the stabilization of the global financial system. For this reason, it wants to renew the commitment credit, so as to make up to 10 billion available in the event of a crisis.
The Federal Council also intends to strengthen cybersecurity through a law regulating software and hardware products, data, and digital infrastructure. The proposal must be drawn up by June 2027. The text thus describes legislative work with a specified deadline.
Finally, Switzerland and the EU have negotiated a new package of agreements to stabilize and develop bilateral relations. The Federal Council submitted the package to Parliament on March 13, 2026. The official Swiss Government page brings together this information with the decisions, activities, and functioning of the Federal Council as a collegial body, as well as popular votes. ## The practical reading for families and savers
The announcements have different timelines and should be separated into effects that are already scheduled and decisions that are still at a later stage. With regard to AVS/AHV pension provision, the closest reference to the cost of living is the evolution of prices and wages. The third pillar also calls for caution. The Government announces an increase in the maximum permitted contribution, but the announcement does not state the new numerical limit. The commitment credit follows a different logic. The Government wants to renew a facility of up to 10 billion so that it can help stabilize the global financial system in the event of a crisis. It is not presented as an automatic payment to families or as an immediate change in income. For the reader, the point to follow is the renewal of the credit and its stated purpose.

## TL;DR - Salathé considers the apocalyptic scenarios exaggerated. - He is a professor at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Lausanne. - Big tech companies are preparing to go public. - The risks cited include military uses and cyberattacks.
## Key facts - Protagonist → Marcel Salathé - Role → is a professor at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Lausanne and co-directs the AI center - Objection → exaggerated scenarios, economic interests and tailor-made rules - Risks → military uses and cyberattacks - Market → companies nearing a stock market listing, with valuations in the trillions
## The voice of dissent
For weeks, tech giants have been multiplying warnings about the risks of uncontrolled artificial intelligence development. But not everyone shares this view. Marcel Salathé, a Swiss scientist and professor at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Lausanne, co-directs the AI center and has described some scenarios as exaggerated. In his view, these messages conceal economic interests and the desire to obtain tailor-made rules.
On the news, Salathé explained that part of the public genuinely fears that new technologies could take over. His question, however, concerns how quickly these fears made it onto the front pages of the Wall Street Journal and the New York Times. The professor said he did not understand why.
### The alarm and its effects
Salathé also took issue with the language used by some researchers in the preceding weeks. He associates the expression “we will all die within ten years” with the way cults speak and considers it dangerous. The concern is that a prediction presented as certainty could drive someone to extreme acts against other people or themselves, including suicide, collective suicides and attacks against those developing these technologies.
The debate thus has two levels. On the one hand, there are warnings about possible extreme scenarios. On the other, there is suspicion that alarmism may function as a market strategy. The source points to companies nearing a stock market listing, with valuations in the trillions. According to Salathé, these companies fear competition from smaller companies, start-ups and China, identified as the leading power in artificial intelligence. In his view, fear would become a tool for obtaining protection.
In the picture presented by the report, Stefano Quintarelli and Marco Zaffalon instead identify social manipulation and concentration of power as real risks. Salathé does not deny every danger: he acknowledges malicious uses, such as military applications and cyberattacks, and notes that the same technology can be used for defense. ## What remains for the Swiss public
The news has a specific Swiss connection, but it does not describe a measure that changes the status of a resident or worker today. The national aspect is the presence of a Swiss researcher at EPFL in a discussion that touches on companies, markets and rules. The source does not indicate amounts, deadlines, obligations or procedures: no automatic effect on daily life can be inferred from this text.
This distinction is useful because the debate mixes different aspects. The first concerns technical risks and malicious uses. The second concerns market power: Salathé links the warnings to the companies' future entry into the stock market and to competition with start-ups, smaller companies and China. The third concerns society: the reference to Stefano Quintarelli and Marco Zaffalon includes social manipulation and concentration of power.
### Three questions for reading the warnings
The first question is who is speaking. An alarm raised by tech giants and an assessment by Salathé do not represent the same perspective. The second is which risk is being described: a cyberattack or military use are concrete examples identified by the professor; the statement about everyone dying within ten years is instead an extreme prediction reported in the piece. The third is what countermeasure is proposed. Salathé argues that the same artificial intelligence can be used for defense.
For those living in Switzerland, the practical result is a rule of caution in reading, not a new application to submit to an office. It is not correct to turn this news into a prediction about personal consequences: the text does not provide those data. Nor does the reference to start-ups amount to a job announcement; anyone who wants to follow that path can consult aziende che assumono. The economic component should therefore be read as a thesis attributed to Salathé, not as a fact independently demonstrated by the source.
For the same reason, the passage about the stock market is not enough to measure an effect on costo della vita in Svizzera.

## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## An operational method for not amplifying the alarm
The source does not provide a deadline or an administrative procedure. The action available to the reader is to verify the content of the statements before turning them into personal conclusions. Five steps are enough, all drawn from the contrast presented in the report.
1. Isolate the sentence. Mark whether the message discusses uncontrolled development, a possible dominance of AI, or the formula about everyone dying within ten years. Do not treat these expressions as equivalent: the source presents them within a controversy over the tone of the alarms.
2. Attribute the voice. Write separately what the tech giants claim, what Marcel Salathé disputes, and what the report says about experts Stefano Quintarelli and Marco Zaffalon. Avoid the generic label of experts if it changes the substance of the claim.
3. Classify the risk. Put military uses and cyberattacks, identified by Salathé as possible malicious uses, in a first box. Place social manipulation and concentration of power in a second. The third box concerns extreme scenarios and the social consequences of alarmism.
4. Look for the countermeasure. Salathé does not describe AI only as a threat: he argues that the same technology can be used for defense. Comparing risk and defense prevents stopping at the most dramatic headline.
5. Separate facts from motivations. The future stock-market listing and competition from startups, smaller companies, and China are part of the explanation proposed by the professor. Present it as his interpretation, not as conclusive proof.
### What not to do
There are no amounts to calculate, documents to prepare, or deadlines to meet in the text. Therefore, there is no need to invent an administrative response or attribute an immediate change to the news for those who live or work in Switzerland. The procedure serves to read the topic better and distinguish threat, market, power, and defense.

## The protest in French-speaking newsrooms
LAUSANNE - Tamedia's French-speaking newsrooms oppose the new cuts announced on Monday by the Zurich-based publisher. Employees are calling for the layoffs to be abandoned and are considering possible forms of mobilization.
Tuesday, the day after the announcement, newsroom members met in a general assembly. The measure affects 41 employees in Switzerland, 13 of them in Lausanne and Geneva. In the press release issued on Wednesday, the staff describes the number of positions affected as considerable: nearly 10% of the company's French-speaking staff.
The entities mentioned include 24 Heures, La Tribune de Genèv, Le Matin Dimanche, Femina and Bilan. The list also includes the Digital, Print and Visual Desk areas, and thus different publications and functions within the company.
### The 2024 precedent
The new staff reduction was unanimously rejected by the assembly, just four days after the end of the moratorium on layoffs agreed in 2024. At that time, 25 positions had already been eliminated in western Switzerland.
In the statement, employees argue that the new cuts would have devastating consequences for the publications. They also criticize the use of artificial intelligence and automation: in their view, these technologies could improve working conditions, but the company would also use them to replace people. The criticism also concerns the growing use of articles not produced on site, simple translations and contributions from abroad, sometimes poorly adapted to local realities.
The staff describes a situation of exhaustion and anger. The layoffs of those who have worked to provide quality journalism are in the firing line, while the managers identified by the employees as responsible for the situation remain in their positions.
Employees consider it unacceptable that the people who have spared no effort to ensure quality journalism should be laid off, while the managers who have led them into a dead end remain in their positions.
For the employees, TX Group — which Tamedia is part of — has the means to invest in journalism. The newsrooms therefore call on Tamedia's management and TX Group's board of directors to abandon the layoffs and open a transparent dialogue about the future of journalism in western Switzerland. ## What it means for work in the sector

## TL;DR - 63rd session of the Human Rights Council in Geneva - Switzerland led a coalition on transitional justice - Privacy and non-discrimination among the criteria for AI - 86 States supported the Swiss appeal to the UN
## Key facts - Publication → October 7, 2026 - Location → Geneva - Body → Human Rights Council - AI → gender equality, non-discrimination and disinformation - Support → 86 States supporting the UN reform appeal
From Bern, the communiqué published on October 7, 2026, reports the conclusion, in Geneva, of the 63rd session of the Human Rights Council. The discussions examined artificial intelligence, the risks it poses to human rights and the opportunities it offers to strengthen respect for them.
In the report, Switzerland is active on two fronts: it committed to resolutions on the impact of AI and led a group of States on transitional justice. The first strand also concerns services explicitly cited by the source, such as human resources management and access to housing.
### AI between equality and disinformation
Switzerland supported two resolutions devoted to the consequences of AI for gender equality, non-discrimination and combating disinformation. Their aim is to curb the circulation of deepfakes and content related to online harassment, phenomena whose spread has been facilitated by new technologies.
The communiqué links these risks to the use of AI in services. It does not limit the issue to the digital sphere in the abstract: it cites human resources management and access to housing. New technologies must be designed in a way that ensures respect for the right to privacy and the principle of non-discrimination.
### Transitional justice and international issues
A second result concerns transitional justice. A coalition of States led by Switzerland enabled the adoption of two resolutions. The four pillars identified are establishing the truth, combating impunity, providing reparation and guaranteeing non-recurrence of violations.
According to the communiqué, examining the past serves to address tensions and prevent violence from resuming. After a war, transitional justice is described as a tool for maintaining peace. New technologies can help document violations and search for missing persons.
During discussions on specific situations, Switzerland supported extending the mandate of the United Nations Special Rapporteur monitoring the human rights situation in Russia, reiterated its condemnation of indiscriminate drone attacks against civilians, denounced sexual violence used as torture against civilians and prisoners of war in Ukraine and supported extending the mandate of the mission tasked with investigating crimes committed during the conflict in Sudan. Regarding reform of the architecture of the UN human rights system, its appeal to harmonize the operating methods of treaty bodies received the support of 86 States. ## The practical meaning for work and home
The most concrete connection with the lives of those who live or work in Switzerland lies in the examples chosen in the statement: human resources management and access to housing. The source does not describe an individual outcome or a procedure to follow; instead, it indicates an approach: when AI is used in services, its design must respect the right to privacy and the principle of non-discrimination.
For work, the practical question is whether the use of AI in human resources management is assessed through these two principles. For housing, the same lens concerns access to the service. The source stops at this approach and does not detail an individual outcome. The passage remains relevant because the statement calls for new technologies to be designed in a way that guarantees specific rights.

The table separates the realm of services from that of transitional justice. In the former, the reader focuses on privacy and non-discrimination; in the latter, on the possibilities offered by new technologies for documenting violations and searching for missing persons. Confusing the two realms would lead to reading every use of AI as if it had the same purpose.
Disinformation and content related to online harassment add another question: does the problem concern the service or the spread of content? The two resolutions on AI referenced by Switzerland address precisely this set of risks.

item.description: Dal primo gennaio chiudono gli sportelli in 13 stazioni.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Starting January 1, ticket offices at 13 stations will close. - Staffed points will decrease from 115 to 102. - 97% of tickets are purchased through self-service channels. - 3% of tickets are still sold at the ticket counter.
## Key facts - When → from January 1st - Closures → 13 stations - Points with staff → 115 today, 102 in three months - Over-the-counter purchases → 3%; in 2019 just under 10% - Self-service purchases → 97%; digital 85%
Starting from January 1st, thirteen other small FFS stations will no longer offer personalized advice: in the last decade the service had already disappeared in around fifty locations. The information was confirmed in writing to Keystone-ATS by Moritz Weisskopf, spokesperson for the SBB, following the news published by the Zurich newspaper Blick.
With the exception of Geneva Eaux-Vives, in the district on the left bank of Lake Geneva, the stations affected from next year are all located in German-speaking Switzerland. Travel Centres, a name used by SBB, will remain available in 102 stations.
The reason given for the reduction in supply is the sharp decline in demand for tickets purchased over the counter. The share dropped to 3%, while in 2019 it was still just under 10%. Today 97% of transport tickets are purchased through self-service channels; the majority, 85%, are purchased digitally through the company's app or website. For SBB, operating manned sales outlets in stations with few customers is not economically sustainable.
The number of staffed sales points was 169 at the end of 2016, it is 115 today and in three months it will be 102. In the worst case, reaching the nearest consultancy point could mean up to 30 minutes of extra travel on mezzi pubblici for customers.
Personal consultation remains available for those who need a special subscription, want to exchange cash or need a certification of authenticity for an important document. The closure of travel centers will not lead to layoffs, according to Weisskopf.
> «There will be no layoffs; the affected employees will be able to continue to carry out their activities in other travel centers". The shift from the counter to self-service mainly changes how assistance is accessed. The network is not described as being without staff: the point is that advice is concentrated in the remaining centers, while the most frequent purchases shift to digital tools or ticket machines.
### Comparing the different needs
| Need indicated by FFS | Channel to use | |---|---| | Purchase of travel tickets | App, website or ticket machine | | Special pass | Staffed counter | | Cash exchange | Staffed counter | | Certification of authenticity for an important document | Staffed counter |
The distinction is practical. Anyone who needs to purchase a ticket through a self-service channel can do so without necessarily looking for a location offering assistance. Anyone who instead needs to carry out one of the operations listed by FFS must continue to go to a counter. The availability of the service therefore depends less on the individual departure station and more on the type of request.
For customers at the stations concerned, the change may mean a longer journey to the nearest travel center. The source indicates, in the worst case, up to 30 additional minutes by public transport. This makes it important to distinguish between an ordinary purchase and a procedure requiring personal assistance, especially when a journey to another location must be arranged.
The plan covers several cantons in German-speaking Switzerland, with the exception of Geneva Eaux-Vives. It therefore does not concern just one area of the network, but stations spread across several cantonal territories. FFS have announced the closures through regional press releases, following customary practice.
The long-term outlook also remains open. Weisskopf has not indicated how many assistance points will be present in 2036 or what their exact setup will be. Today, FFS tend to strengthen the remaining travel centers. Anyone who wants to separate the effect of travel from other daily expenses can consult costo della vita in Svizzera.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ### Practical procedure
1. Check the relevant location. FFS announced the closures through regional press releases. For an affected station, the first step is therefore to check whether the staffed location is included in the published list. 2. Determine the type of transaction. Purchasing transport tickets falls under the use of self-service channels; a special pass, cash exchange or authenticity certification, on the other hand, requires assistance at the counter. 3. Use the digital channel when it is sufficient. The FFS app and website are identified by the source as channels through which tickets are purchased in digital format. Alternatively, ticket machines are available. 4. Plan the journey for matters requiring personal assistance. If the usual station no longer offers assistance, another travel centre must be reached. In the worst case, the journey by public transport may take up to 30 minutes longer.
For those who need to go to a counter, distinguishing between the different requests avoids starting from the assumption that every service is available online. The source expressly indicates that some needs will continue to require a staffed location. The digital channel is therefore a solution for purchasing tickets, not a general substitute for assistance.
For staff too, the situation described by FFS is handled differently from that of customers: closing a travel centre does not entail layoffs, and the affected employees can continue their work at other travel centres. For users, however, the operational point of reference remains the location where the necessary assistance is available.
There is no fixed configuration of the network through 2036. Weisskopf explained that it is not currently possible to predict with certainty how many service points will be present then. It is therefore advisable to check regional communications before handling a matter that requires staff, rather than considering access to the counter stable.

## TL;DR - BNS: foreign currency reserves at 771 billion - In September, +0,4 billion compared with August - Euro +0,9%, dollar +3%; together about 80%
## Key facts - Foreign-exchange reserves: 771 billion francs - Monthly change: 0,4 billion more - Total reserves, excluding gold: from 782 to 783 billion - Exchange rates at the end of September: euro 0,9458 and dollar 0,8328 francs - Share of the euro and dollar: around 80% of foreign-exchange reserves
At the end of September, the foreign-exchange reserves held by the Swiss National Bank stood at 771 billion francs, 0,4 billion more than in August. The SNB therefore describes the monthly movement as essentially stable. The information was published on the institution's website; the text is preceded by the attribution (Keystone-ATS).
### The SNB's monthly figure
The figure relating solely to foreign-exchange reserves should be considered alongside that for total reserves, excluding gold. This item went from 782 to 783 billion francs. The source gives both amounts, but relates them to two aggregates named differently: to read the bulletin without confusing them, the figure of 771 billion must be kept separate from that of 783 billion.
The SNB's message does not attribute the September figure to a single cause. The institution notes that fluctuations are not unusual and that they often have to do with developments in foreign-exchange markets. It adds that they may also be the result of monetary-policy measures. The reference to the markets and monetary policy explains why the month-on-month comparison should not be read as a simple isolated addition or subtraction.
The statistics show a strengthening of the two currencies that together account for around 80% of foreign-exchange reserves. The euro rose to 0,9458 francs from 0,9378 at the end of August, a change of 0,9%. The US dollar went from 0,8089 to 0,8328 francs, strengthening by 3%. To follow the comparison between the euro and the franc at the two points in time, one can use comparatore CHF/EUR, keeping the exchange rate and the amount of the reserves distinct.
The historical context mentioned by the source also concerns the institution's leadership: since October 2024, the executive management has been chaired by Martin Schlegel. For several years, the SNB purchased large quantities of foreign currency, especially after abandoning, at the beginning of 2015, the minimum exchange-rate threshold against the euro. These are the elements given to place the monthly figure in context, without adding a new decision to the communiqué. ## Practical reading
The most useful way to read the figures is to separate the change in reserves from the change in exchange rates. In the first case, one looks at the move from August to September; in the second, at the quotations of the euro and the dollar expressed in francs. The source places the two pieces of information in the same framework, but does not attribute the movement in reserves to a single explanation: it refers to foreign exchange markets and, alternatively, monetary policy measures.
### Three aspects not to confuse
| Indicator | September figure | Comparison indicated | |---|---:|---| | Foreign currency reserves | 771 billion francs | 0,4 billion more than in August | | Total reserves, excluding gold | 783 billion | from 782 billion | | Euro | 0,9458 francs | from 0,9378; +0,9% | | US dollar | 0,8328 francs | from 0,8089; +3% |
The comparison shows that stability in the amount does not mean an absence of movement in exchange rates. Foreign currency reserves increased by 0,4 billion, while the euro and the dollar recorded the changes indicated by the statistics. The reader should therefore avoid substituting one number for the other: 771 billion is the value of foreign currency reserves; 0,9458 and 0,8328 are quotations in francs.
The excluding-gold entry also requires attention. The move from 782 to 783 billion refers to total reserves excluding gold, not to the same row as foreign currency reserves alone. This is a lexical and numerical distinction already present in the BNS communication, useful for comparing August and September without adding up different items.
The data on the two main exchange rates helps explain why the source refers to foreign exchange markets: the euro and the dollar together account for about 80% of foreign currency reserves. This data alone is not enough, however, to establish which component produced the change of 0,4 billion, because the BNS also mentions monetary policy measures. The causal relationship is not specified for September.

1. Start with the period. Write September as the month of the observation and August as the comparison period. Next to the main figure, note that the amount of foreign exchange reserves is expressed in billions of francs and that the indicated monthly difference is 0,4 billion.

## TL;DR - Ten-year Confederation bonds yield 0,58% - The SNB keeps the policy rate at 0% - The yield has risen from 0,18% to 0,69% - Inflation is at 1%, between 0% and 2%
## Key facts - Current ten-year yield → 0,58% - SNB policy rate → 0% - Yield in 2026 → from 0,18% to 0,69% - Inflation and SNB target range → 1% / between 0% and 2%
The 0,58% yield on ten-year Swiss Confederation bonds is the central figure in the movement observed in Switzerland. Although the SNB is keeping its policy rate at 0%, the yield paid to those financing the state is now significantly higher than in the recent past.
After hitting the annual low of 0,18% at the beginning of the war in Iran, the yield on the so-called «Eidgenossen» rose to 0,69% at the end of September, the high for 2026, and now stands at 0,58%.
### Why the ten-year maturity reacts Swiss yields follow global dynamics, albeit in attenuated form. They are driven above all by developments in international bond markets: the SNB sets the cost of money in the short term, but does not directly determine the yield on ten-year bonds.
Longer-term bonds are affected by expectations for future monetary policy, inflation, growth, the state of public finances and demand for bonds.
> «The Swiss bond market is not completely immune to international interest-rate movements, but it reacts in a much more muted way than the major foreign markets,» Markus Thöny, an expert at Lombard Odier Investment Managers, explains to the Awp news agency.
In September, inflation in the Confederation reached 1%, the highest level in the past two years, driven mainly by energy costs; the figure nevertheless remained within the SNB's target range, between 0% and 2%. The franc also has a special role: when uncertainty rises, demand for this currency may increase. The appreciation of the franc helps contain prices, but penalizes exports.
Switzerland also benefits from relatively sound public finances. Therefore, unlike the United States, France and Japan, the rise in yields does not signal growing concerns about debt sustainability. In the United States, the size of the deficits, the large volume of government bonds on offer and uncertainty over inflation and growth are weighing; in Europe, spending needs for infrastructure and defense weigh, while in Japan the central bank has begun normalization after decades of ultra-expansionary monetary policy. ## The practical meaning for those following Switzerland The ten-year figure should not be read as an automatic reflection of the policy rate. item.title: Prostate cancer: good care in Switzerland 2020–2023
item.description: Oltre 35'000 casi analizzati tra il 2020 e il 2023
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - More than 35'000 cases analyzed between 2020 and 2023 - 8'929 new cases and 1'340 average annual deaths - 76% is detected through opportunistic screening - Three-year survival: 97%
## Key facts - Cases analyzed → more than 35'000 - Period → 2020-2023 - Average new cases per year → 8'929 - Average deaths per year → 1'340 - Opportunistic screening → 76% - Tumor board → 56% - One-year survival → 99% - Three-year survival → 97%
### The picture emerging from the registries
ZURICH - More than 35'000 cases of prostate cancer diagnosed between 2020 and 2023 were examined in the first national analysis of indicators for diagnosis and treatment. The work was carried out by the National Cancer Registration Service (SNRT), together with the Swiss Society of Urology (Swiss Urology).
The report assesses care positively: compared with other European countries, Switzerland has low mortality and high survival rates. During the same period, there were an average of 8'929 new cases and 1'340 deaths per year. Among men, it is the most frequently diagnosed neoplasm in the country.
76% of cases are identified through opportunistic screening; 13% of diagnoses arise from an incidental finding and 7% from symptoms. As age increases, the share of incidental discoveries or those related to symptoms rises.
Opportunistic screening includes the PSA test, that is, prostate-specific antigen; doctor and patient weigh its advantages and disadvantages and decide on a case-by-case basis whether to perform it. In Switzerland, there is no national systematic and uniform screening program for this cancer; for breast and colon cancer, however, screening is organized at national level.
### Stages and risk
36% of tumors are diagnosed at stage I and 30% at stage II, when the disease is still limited to the prostate. 14% of cases belong to risk group 1, while a further 14% are classified in group 2a: for both categories, the risk of progression is limited.
The report does, however, point out the downside of early diagnosis. Especially in older men, tumors may emerge that would not have acquired clinical relevance or reduced life expectancy. For those with a limited life expectancy, screening tests should therefore be used with caution.
For low-risk tumors confined to the prostate, the strategy normally indicated is active surveillance, not immediate treatment. In risk group 1, it concerns about 72% of patients and involves close monitoring with PSA, magnetic resonance imaging and biopsy. For the separate issue of health insurance coverage, guide LAMal/cassa malati is available. ### Risk-calibrated therapies
The crux of the analysis concerns low-risk tumors: in 20% of cases, treatment is nevertheless pursued, such as surgery or radiotherapy, instead of active surveillance. According to the report, many of these treatments would likely be avoidable: compared with active surveillance, they would provide no additional benefits and could cause side effects.
The proposal put forward by the authors is uniform, evidence-based screening, with clear inclusion and exclusion criteria. Such an approach could limit both overdiagnosis and overtreatment, keeping distinct the need to detect the disease early from the risk of treating tumors that would not have had clinical significance.
Among all patients, radical prostatectomy is the most common intervention and concerns 35% of cases. Hormone therapy was administered to 25%, while 19% received radiotherapy. The possible combination of the different options depends on the characteristics of the tumor, the patient's condition and the therapeutic objective.
In tumors with intermediate to high risk, surgery is used in 37%-57% of cases. Radiotherapy, with or without hormone therapy and/or additional chemotherapy, concerns 17%-43%. When distant metastases are already present at the time of diagnosis, hormone therapy and/or chemotherapy alone is used in 69% of cases. These data refer to different clinical groups, not to a single pathway applicable to everyone.
### Multidisciplinary discussion
In 56% of cases, the treatment decision is made by an oncology committee, or tumor board. Within it, specialists from different disciplines discuss the options and formulate recommendations in line with the most up-to-date treatment standards.
The report recommends that, whenever possible, every new diagnosis of prostate cancer be reviewed by one of these committees. Collegial discussion is identified as a tool to improve care and reduce the risk of excessive treatment. For separate in-depth information on health coverage, guide LAMal/cassa malati is available.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ### Five operational steps
The report can also be read as an operational framework for navigating diagnosis, monitoring and treatment decisions. The sequence follows the elements indicated in the analysis.
1. Define how the disease was identified: opportunistic screening, incidental finding or symptoms. The distribution changes with age, because the proportion of incidental or symptom-related diagnoses increases.
2. Place the PSA test within the individual discussion between doctor and patient. The advantages and disadvantages are assessed before deciding whether to perform it, in the absence of a systematic and uniform national program for prostate cancer.
3. Consider stage and risk together. The disease may still be confined to the prostate, while risk groups 1 and 2a are described as having a limited risk of progression. These elements distinguish low-risk cases from the others.
4. In low-risk cases confined to the prostate, assess the active surveillance pathway, which includes close monitoring with PSA tests, magnetic resonance imaging and biopsy. In older men with limited life expectancy, the report recommends caution in the use of screening.
5. Check the multidisciplinary step: the recommendation is that every new diagnosis be discussed, whenever possible, by an oncology committee. The tumor board brings together specialists from different disciplines to assess the options and formulate recommendations according to the most recent treatment standards.
This framework keeps separate two objectives that the report presents together: early diagnosis, which is beneficial for treatment and prognosis, and the reduction of unnecessary findings or therapies. Relative survival is calculated in relation to the general population: 99% one year after diagnosis, 98% after two years and 97% after three years. The report places these figures alongside a low mortality rate compared with the rest of Europe. For a separate in-depth look at healthcare coverage, consult LAMal/cassa malati.

## TL;DR - October 5, 2026: Parmelin meets Indian leaders - Switzerland and India sign two agreements - TEPA: one year since its entry into force with EFTA - AI summit in Geneva in spring 2027
## Key facts - Date → 5 October 2026 - Location → New Delhi - Meetings → Guy Parmelin, Droupadi Murmu and Narendra Modi - Agreements → migration and exchange of young professionals - Negotiator → State Secretariat for Migration (SEM) - Trade framework → TEPA between India and EFTA States - Next summit → Geneva AI summit, spring 2027 - Economic event → Prosperity Summit India-EFTA, 7 October
## Agreements and visit agenda
On 5 October 2026, in New Delhi, President of the Swiss Confederation Guy Parmelin held talks with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Indian President Droupadi Murmu, as well as with other representatives of the Indian government. The talks with Modi focused on economic exchanges and cooperation in education and research.
The state visit took place ahead of the eightieth anniversary of diplomatic relations between Switzerland and India, which will be celebrated in 2028. Trade policy occupied a central place at the summit: the visit coincided with the first anniversary of the entry into force of the TEPA between India and the EFTA States.
Both sides described the TEPA as a positive signal in an era of global uncertainty and stressed that implementation is proceeding according to plan. Parmelin highlighted the strong interest of Swiss companies in the Indian market.
The talks covered the new bilateral agreement on investment protection, whose negotiations are at an advanced stage, as well as issues relating to the protection of intellectual property. In the scientific field, the President of the Swiss Confederation confirmed his commitment to making the partnership even stronger.
### Migration, mobility and young workers
Switzerland and India expressed their appreciation for the two agreements concluded through negotiations conducted by the State Secretariat for Migration (SEM). The partnership on migration and mobility strengthens the already well-established cooperation between the two countries and expands exchanges in the fields of education, science and the labour market, while also supporting legal mobility. It also provides rules for the readmission of people required to leave the country and joint initiatives against irregular entry, human trafficking and document forgery.
The second agreement, dedicated to the exchange of young workers, allows young citizens of the two countries to undertake a period of training or further education in the other country, fostering the development of their professional and linguistic skills.
### The international agenda
During their talks, Parmelin and Modi examined the development of artificial intelligence and also discussed democracy, geopolitics, the UN and multilateralism. For Switzerland, the AI summit planned in Geneva for spring 2027 follows in the footsteps of the one organised by India this year. The programme also includes meetings in the economic sphere, a visit to Noida International Airport, which is managed by a subsidiary of Zurich Airport, an event on scientific cooperation and the second Prosperity Summit India-EFTA, scheduled for 7 October. ## The practical implications of the two agreements
The communiqué allows a concrete reading for those who live or work in Switzerland: the relationship with India is structured through different channels, each with a clearly identifiable objective. The first agreement concerns migration and mobility; the second concerns young workers and training or further-education stays. Separating the two areas prevents every initiative from being read as a generic opening of the labor market.
### The distinction that matters to citizens and businesses
For a young Swiss or Indian citizen, the practical point of reference is the exchange that allows a stay in the other State. The outcome indicated by the source is not only the training experience: it also includes professional and language skills. The migration component, by contrast, has a broader scope and includes training, science, the labor market and legal mobility, along with readmission and cooperation against irregular migration, human trafficking and document forgery. The two agreements complement each other, but they do not serve the same purpose.
For Swiss companies, the key dossiers to follow are TEPA implementation, investment protection and intellectual property protection. The communiqué presents implementation of the agreement as proceeding according to plan and the investment negotiations as advanced: for this reason, it is advisable to distinguish what is already covered by TEPA from what remains the subject of bilateral talks. The visit by the business delegation and the stop at Noida International Airport, managed by a subsidiary of Aeroporto di Zurich, also give the mission a business dimension.
For research, the focus is different: scientific cooperation was reaffirmed, and the program includes a high-level event. Artificial intelligence adds an international dimension, linked to the Geneva summit in spring 2027 and to the role of the UN and multilateralism. For Switzerland, therefore, the agenda is not only commercial.
| Area | Practical reading | |---|---| | Young workers | Training or further education in the other State; professional and language skills | | Migration and mobility | Exchanges in training, science and the labor market; legal mobility and cooperation | | Business and research | TEPA, investment, intellectual property and scientific partnership |
