Those who live or work in Switzerland and want to understand which of the two agreements concerns them can turn the communiqué into a small working framework. The aim is to direct each question to the correct channel and keep training, mobility, business and research separate.
### Four operational steps
1. Define the topic. A question about migration, legal mobility, readmission or cooperation against irregular migration should be linked to the partnership on migration and mobility. A question about a training or professional development stay for young citizens should be linked to the agreement on the exchange of young workers.
2. Clarify the objective of the request. In the text devoted to young workers, the source indicates the promotion of professional and language skills. In the migration partnership, by contrast, the scope also includes training, science and the labor market. This distinction makes the question to be submitted to SEM more precise.
3. Separate the economic dimension from the individual one. If the matter concerns a Swiss company, the topics indicated are the implementation of TEPA, investment protection, intellectual property and scientific cooperation. If it concerns a young person, the reference remains the training or professional development stay in the other state. These are not the same path.
4. Use the contact indicated in the communiqué. For questions relating to the Migration and Mobility Partnership and the agreement on the exchange of young workers, the source indicates SEM Information and Communication at medien@sem.admin.ch. In the message, it is advisable to specify which of the two agreements is of interest and whether the matter concerns mobility, training or professional exchange.
### The next dates to follow
On the mission's calendar, the second Prosperity Summit India-AELS is scheduled for October 7 and brings together government and business representatives to discuss new investment and cooperation opportunities. The Geneva AI summit, on the other hand, is scheduled for spring 2027. Keeping these two appointments distinct helps follow the economic dossier and the technology dossier separately. ## TL;DR - FiberMotor: diameter from 1 to 3 millimeters - Four motors lift a 46-gram bar - The prototype was integrated into a pair of trousers - A start-up aims to commercialize the technology
## Key facts - Development → EPFL research team - Structure → two hollow fibers with copper wires - Publication → Advanced Materials journal - Initial goal → greater power and durability
### The prototype presented in Lausanne
The FiberMotor, a thread-like motor, was developed by a research group at the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Lausanne (EPFL). In a note, the institute specified that the device measures one to three millimeters in diameter. The description of the device was published in the specialist journal Advanced Materials.
The device consists of two hollow fibers, one positioned inside the other. Thin copper wires wrap around both. Applying an electrical voltage causes electrostatic forces to push them closer together. Consequently, the inner fiber moves back and forth inside the outer one.
### Movement without gears
The construction distinguishes FiberMotor from the traditional motors described by the researchers. The device does not need gears and does not require mechanical transmission of force. For this reason, it is flexible and can also be moved from the outside. If, for example, an arm is moved in the opposite direction to that generated by the motor, the device does not lock up.
Four combined motors produced enough force to lift a 46-gram chocolate bar. This is the measurement reported for the test described by EPFL.
### From the pants test to the start-up
One of the applications mentioned is a wearable robotic suit intended to help people walk. As a demonstration, the researchers integrated the motors into a pair of pants. The idea for the future is to insert many of these thin motors into clothing, making them work like threads. Together they could support movement when the leg bends or extends.
To bring the technology toward commercialization, the researchers have already founded a start-up. Initially, they want to make the motor more powerful and more durable. The source does not indicate a date for commercialization: the project is presented through the prototype, the pants test, and the development goals indicated by the team. ## From research to possible use
For those following research in Switzerland, the news should be read as a step toward an application, not as the announcement of a product already available. The source sets out a component developed by EPFL, a test on a garment, and the founding of a start-up. The practical value lies in understanding what has already been done and what remains stated as an objective.
### Three levels to distinguish
The first level is the form factor. A motor with a diameter of one to three millimeters can be described as thin; the source adds that it is flexible and can be moved from the outside. It is not merely a matter of reducing the dimensions: the absence of gears and a mechanical transmission allows the device to follow an opposing movement without locking up. The researchers link this characteristic to the possibility of inserting it into clothing like a thread.
The second level is the test. Four units lifted a 46-gram chocolate bar. This is a measurable result of the combined system, but it is not equivalent to describing a full suit. ## TL;DR - TCS compares prices at 19’000 Swiss charging points - 50 kWh cost between 23 and 46 francs - 5% of charging takes place at fast-charging stations - The app shows availability and price according to the profile
## Key facts - Tool → TCS free radar - Coverage → 19’000 charging points in Switzerland - Fast charging → 50 kWh - Cost → 23-46 francs - Home charging → 29 centimes per kilowatt-hour on average - Slow-charging power → 11 kilowatts - Platforms → iOS and Android - Charging-station status → green, red or grey
The Touring Club Svizzero has introduced a free radar that allows users to compare the rates of 19’000 charging points distributed throughout the Confederation. In the On en parle program of October 5, 2026, broadcast on RTS Première at 08.33, the radar is described as a tool for navigating a market whose rates are often far from transparent. The initiative aims to guide drivers, as has already happened with fossil fuels.
TCS tests show the possible difference for a fast 50 kWh charge: an amount sufficient for around 300 kilometres in a mid-size car can cost between 23 and 46 francs. The range is almost double.
> Speaking to RTS, Moreno Volpi, a member of the TCS management, stressed: «It is almost double».
At service stations, the price per litre is displayed; for charging stations, however, activation fees and per-minute charges may be added to the cost per kilowatt-hour, while subscriptions have varying conditions. To compare offers, it is therefore necessary to consider the final price, not just the cost per kilowatt-hour.
Available for iOS and Android, the free TCS app compares electricity prices with those of petrol and diesel. Users can create a profile specifying charging speed, subscription type and operator. The system displays the nearest charging stations and their availability in real time: green indicates those that are free, red those that are occupied, while grey indicates that the information is unavailable.
### A single radar for Swiss networks
For each point, the system indicates the connector type, power and total rate calculated according to the user’s personal profile. TCS also specifies that, unlike Swiss Charge, the radar brings together all operators present in Switzerland. A feature for reporting faults, price differences and new charging stations not yet catalogued is planned by the end of the year. ## How much does the choice matter in everyday life
The first practical distinction is between charging at home or at work and fast charging during a journey. In Switzerland, home charging remains the cheapest option: an average of 29 cents per kilowatt-hour, especially when the car is plugged in at night. The TCS says that slow charging at 11 kilowatts is sufficient to fill the battery overnight.
### Home, work and public charging
For those who have this option, this figure shifts the comparison from the price of an individual charging station to the routine. Several companies allow their employees to charge during working hours. Those who cannot do so at home can therefore consider their workplace or destinations they frequent, instead of automatically relying on fast charging.
Only 5% of charging takes place at fast-charging stations, used mainly for long journeys. The figure suggests a concrete difference between everyday use and trips: in the former case, planning where to plug in the car matters; in the latter, waiting time, the final price and subscription terms become more important.
### When the journey changes the calculation
For those who often use fast charging, whether in everyday life or while travelling, TCS identifies monthly subscriptions as a possible way to save money. The operators mentioned include Ionity, Electra, Tesla and Fastned. Prices tend to be higher on motorways, but the result depends on the subscription: it is therefore not enough to look for the nearest charging station or automatically lengthen the route.
For electric cars, there is no fixed formula analogous to the «3x5» for conventional fuels. That criterion considers it worthwhile to add 5 kilometers to the journey when the saving is at least 5 cents and at least 50 liters are refueled. On long journeys, however, time may matter more than distance: fast charging may be completed in a few dozen minutes, while slow charging may take several hours; no one wants to wait four hours on the motorway.
Range also matters: according to TCS, it is advisable to choose a vehicle capable of providing 2-3 days of typical use within a charge range between 20% and 80%. This reduces dependence on daily charging stations. At the cantonal and municipal levels, financial incentives are also available for assessing buildings and installing basic infrastructure in garages. ### Four operational steps
1. Search in advance. Anyone who cannot charge at home should open the app and check the stations near their home, workplace or frequented destinations. Planning daily AC charging makes it possible to start from an already familiar network instead of looking for a solution at the last minute.
2. Set up the profile. In the free TCS app, you indicate your preferred charging speed, subscription type and operator. If fast charging is frequent, the comparison should also include a monthly subscription, including the options available from Ionity, Electra, Tesla, Fastned or another provider.
3. Check the charging station. Before setting off, check real-time availability: green means available, red means occupied, and grey means the information is unavailable. Once the destination has been selected, check the connector type, power and final price calculated by the radar based on your profile. This allows the app to compare different operators, not just the network of a single provider.
4. Choose the right time. For a long journey, charging speed becomes the main criterion. Fast charging takes about 30-40 minutes, while slow charging can take several hours. The waiting time can be used to reply to emails, take an online language course, walk the dog or listen to a podcast, as TCS suggests.
### Daily checks to carry out
For those who charge in a garage, many cantons and municipalities provide financial incentives to assess buildings and install basic infrastructure. Those who use a car for work can instead check whether their employer allows charging during working hours. Both measures are separate from choosing a fast-charging station and are intended to reduce reliance on public charging stops.
By the end of the year, TCS plans to activate a feature for reporting faults, price differences and new charging stations that have not yet been catalogued. Once it is available, drivers will also be able to use the radar to help update the information. The operational criterion remains simple: set up the profile, check the price and availability before setting off, and choose the solution that fits the time available.

BERN – On November 29, voters will return to the polls to vote on four new ballot measures. The ballot includes an issue linking the VAT increase to the 13th AVS pension, two popular initiatives, and a legislative amendment.

item.description: Il diesel in Svizzera sfiora 2,50 franchi al litro
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Diesel in Switzerland is nearing 2,50 francs per litre - Cressier supplies around 35% of the country's fuel supply - European refining has limited capacity - G7 reserves are a buffer, not a solution
## Key facts - Plant operator → Varopreem - Refinery → Cressier (NE), the only one in Switzerland - Coverage → approximately 35% of national fuel consumption - Operating rate → nearly full capacity - Last new refinery in the United States → 1977 - Last new refinery in Europe → 1975 - Plants closed in Europe since the beginning of the century → more than 30 - Demand → could decrease if prices remain high in 2027
## The alarm from the Cressier refinery
Diesel in Switzerland now sells for almost 2,50 francs per litre. Raising the alarm is Dev Sanyal, CEO of Varopreem, the company entrusted with managing Switzerland's only refinery, in Cressier (NE). In an interview published by the Neue Zürcher Zeitung, the manager describes a combination of record prices, limited refining capacity and geopolitical uncertainty in Europe.
For those following costo della vita in Svizzera, the price at the pump is the most visible signal, but it does not by itself tell the whole story of the refiners' situation. Sanyal links the current phase to the rigidity of the global fuel supply system: for years, he explains, efficiency dominated decision-making; now resilience carries much more weight.
> «These are absolutely extraordinary times: I have been working in this sector for 38 years and I have never experienced a situation like the current one»
The rise at the pump does not automatically translate into higher margins for refiners. Input costs have also increased in the market, while differences in crude oil qualities and transport costs also have an impact. Sanyal also brings 30 years of experience at the British giant BP, a factor informing his reading of the current cycle.
### Cressier at the heart of national production
The group is not directly active in retail sales or in the management of service stations. It does, however, control the Cressier refinery: the facility covers approximately 35% of national fuel consumption and operates nearly at full capacity. The facility is therefore a national link in the chain, but it does not eliminate the difficulties coming from the European market.
The CEO urges people not to consider a good half-year a guarantee for the entire year: the possible obstacles remain numerous. Among the scenarios mentioned is a possible ban by the United States on diesel exports. The effect would be immediate on European markets, with another sharp increase in prices and a shock to supplies that have so far also been supported by US exports.
The release of additional strategic reserves by the G7 countries has reduced the risk of an immediate deterioration and may help ease some of the pressure on supply and prices. Sanyal considers them a buffer, not the solution to the shortage of refining capacity. ## Prices, reserves and capacity: the Swiss perspective
The practical issue for Switzerland is not just how much a litre costs, but how quickly an external problem can feed through to consumer prices and industry. Sanyal sees the Confederation's ability to withstand high prices as an advantage over many Asian and African nations; this does not, however, shield it from the economic effects.
The transformation of the sector helps to understand the risk. Refinery closures could have seemed economically justified: the global market was supposed to prevent shortages. Governments also considered these plants not critical infrastructure but rather relics of the past destined to become redundant with the energy transition. Since the beginning of the century, more than 30 have been closed in Europe.
### The comparison between an efficient market and a resilient market
That choice reduced available capacity just as geopolitical uncertainties are putting routes and facilities under pressure. The war between Iran and Israel and Ukrainian attacks have rendered refineries in the Gulf region and Russia unusable. If bottlenecks around the Strait of Hormuz or in Russia are added, the interview speaks of a perfect storm.
| Signal | Effect indicated by the interview |\n|---|---|\n| G7 strategic reserves | They reduce the risk of an immediate worsening and somewhat ease pressure on supply and prices. |\n| U.S. halt on diesel exports | Shock for European markets and a further sharp increase in prices. |\n| Bottlenecks near the Strait of Hormuz or in Russia | This would result in a highly critical scenario, and a physical shortage cannot be ruled out. |\n| High prices in 2027 as well | European demand could decline. |
Demand behavior confirms that the market has not yet shown a clear trend: after about eight months of war in Iran, Sanyal does not detect a significant change in European diesel and petrol consumption. However, high prices persisting in 2027 would change the scenario, with a possible contraction in demand.
To assess the impact on a personal budget without confusing the consumer price with refining costs, this analysis can be considered alongside busta paga svizzera. The figure to watch is not just today's price, but the duration of the shock and how supply, costs and demand move together.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to follow developments without confusing the signals
To follow the risk without turning every news item into a forecast, those who live or work in Switzerland can use a simple sequence. The method separates the data observed at the pump, industrial costs, and events capable of altering supply.
### Four operational steps
1. **Set the starting point.** The reference is the price of diesel at the pump, almost 2,50 francs per liter. It should be read as a cost for the consumer, not as automatic proof of higher profits for refiners.
2. Separate price and cost structure. In the case described by Sanyal, higher prices also correspond to higher input costs. Differences in crude quality and transport can change the refinery's outcome, so the change at the pump and the industrial margin are not the same thing.
3. Check supply signals. The release of G7 reserves reduces the risk of immediate worsening but acts as a buffer. A possible United States ban on diesel exports, by contrast, would be a shock for Europe. Bottlenecks around the Strait of Hormuz or in Russia are described as a perfect storm, and a physical shortage cannot be ruled out.
4. Distinguish the short and medium term. The CEO does not predict how long the problems will last. If prices remained high also in 2027, European demand could decline; even after a possible resolution of the crisis in Hormuz, a premium linked to operators' perceived risk could remain in crude oil.
This framework is also useful for reading the situation at the national level. Switzerland is better positioned than many Asian and African nations in its ability to pay high prices, but Sanyal nonetheless points to major effects on consumer prices and industry. For a family or a business, therefore, monitoring should not stop at a single refueling: it is worth observing whether the event concerns reserves, refining, or international routes, because the duration of the problem changes the economic pressure.
The final step is to translate fuel spending into disposable income, without introducing forecasts about the duration of the crisis that Sanyal does not venture. For this check, use calcolatore stipendio.

item.title: MPS justice initiatives rejected by the Grand Council
item.description: The Grand Council rejected the two MPS initiatives: reducing magistrates' retirement age from 70 to 65 years (41 votes against) and transferring dismissals to Parliament (61 votes against).
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Two MPS initiatives rejected by the Grand Council - Age of magistrates: proposal to lower it from 70 to 65 - First initiative rejected with 41 votes - Second initiative rejected with 61 votes ## Key facts - Location → Bellinzona - Proponents → Matteo Pronzini and Pino Sergi - First proposal → retirement age from 70 to 65 - Vote on the first proposal → rejected with 41 votes - Current authority for dismissals → Judicial Council - Vote on the second proposal → rejected with 61 votes - Opinions cited → Judicial Council and Court of Appeal In Bellinzona, the Grand Council rejected two MPS-backed justice initiatives. The first concerned the retirement age of magistrates: Matteo Pronzini and Pino Sergi called for lowering it from 70 to 65. The Justice and Rights Committee had consulted the Judicial Council. In a letter sent in May, the latter stated that it considered the current limit appropriate. In its opinion, it cited the experience acquired over the years, the absence of age-related problems and the risk of making the profession less attractive. The initiative was rejected with 41 votes. ### The issue of dismissals The second proposal sought to amend the law on judicial organization. The Grand Council would have had to decide on the dismissal of magistrates, upon a proposal by the Judicial Council. The stated aim was to apply the principle: > “Whoever elects must also dismiss” The initiative apparently also arose following the case involving the dismissal of Siro Quadri and Francesca Verda Chiocchetti. The current framework remains one in which the Judicial Council may order dismissals. According to the report of the Justice and Rights Committee, transferring the authority would have weakened disciplinary oversight and could have created problems regarding the right to appeal. The committee majority therefore called for leaving the law unchanged. The Council of State also, based on the opinions of the Court of Appeal and the Judicial Council, called for maintaining the current system. The Government pointed to the risk of weakening disciplinary powers, the fact that the parliamentary decision could not be appealed before the Appeals Commission on the Judiciary, and the possible confusion between high-level parliamentary oversight and oversight of the judiciary. The second initiative was rejected with 61 votes. ## What remains unchanged after the double no The result has a precise but limited effect: the framework described in the news report remains unchanged with regard to the two issues put to a parliamentary vote. For the first dossier, the reduction in magistrates' retirement age does not pass. For the second, the transfer to the Grand Council of the decision on dismissals does not pass. The distinction matters because the two initiatives addressed different aspects. The first concerned the age limit for the profession. The second, instead, concerned the allocation of the disciplinary function and the relationship between parliamentary oversight and oversight of the judiciary. ### Comparison between the proposal and the current system | Issue | Stated arrangement | Proposed change | Outcome | |---|---|---|---| | Retirement age | Current limit of 70 years | Reduction to 65 years | Rejected with 41 votes | | Dismissal of magistrates | May be ordered by the Judicial Council | Decision by the Grand Council on a proposal from the Judicial Council | Rejected with 61 votes | In the second dossier, the operational issue raised by the commission and the Government was the soundness of disciplinary oversight. The amendment could have weakened the powers of the Judicial Council; moreover, according to the Council of State, a decision by Parliament would not have been appealable before the Appeals Commission on the Judiciary. Assigning a disciplinary function to the Grand Council would also have risked confusing high-level parliamentary oversight with oversight of the judiciary and compromising the separation of powers. For those who live or work in Switzerland, the news does not indicate automatic effects on salaries, taxes, premiums or other items in the family budget. The comparison with the costo della vita in Svizzera must also be kept separate: the vote concerns two rules on the judiciary, not an amount or a benefit described in the source. The practical point is therefore institutional. The reasons cited in support of maintaining the current system remain the reference point for the debate, while neither of the two proposed amendments becomes part of the arrangement described. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to follow the dossier without confusing the issues The source does not indicate deadlines, forms or obligations for citizens and workers. There is therefore no personal administrative procedure to initiate after the vote. The concrete action consists in reading the two initiatives separately and always checking which competence is under discussion. ### A four-step checklist 1. Start with the subject. If the text talks about retirement age and the change from 70 to 65 years, it concerns the first initiative. If it talks about removal, the law on the organization of the judiciary or the principle that whoever elects must also remove, it concerns the second. 2. Check the authority involved. For the first dossier, the Justice and Rights Committee requested an opinion from the Judicial Council. For the second, it is necessary to distinguish the current power to order removal from the proposal to entrust the decision to the Grand Council. 3. Separate the reasons. In the age dossier, record the experience acquired over the years, the absence of age-related problems and the risk of making the profession less attractive. In the removal dossier, instead check disciplinary oversight, the right of appeal and the separation of powers. 4. Note the outcome without turning a proposal into a rule. The first initiative was rejected by 41 votes, the second by 61. The Council of State had invited people to maintain the current system on the basis of the opinions of the Court of Appeal and the Judicial Council. This method avoids attributing disciplinary competence to the Grand Council that the proposal did not introduce into the framework described. It also avoids interpreting the Government's opinion as new legislation: it was a position in favor of maintaining the current system. Any personal tax checks remain separate from this dossier and can be carried out in the section dedicated to dichiarazione delle imposte. item.title: Geneva launches popular vote on CERN's future
item.description: The FCC would be 91 km long, would cost 15 billion francs, and 5’696 signatures are needed by mid-February 2027; final decision by the 25 Member States scheduled for May 2028.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Co-CERNés calls for a popular vote on major CERN projects - The FCC under consideration would be 91 kilometers long - The estimated cost is 15 billion francs - 5’696 signatures are needed by mid-February 2027 ## Key facts - Initiative → cantonal constitutional - Promoters → Co-CERNés coalition - Project → Future Circular Collider (FCC) - Successor to the LHC → from 2045 - Signatures required → 5’696 valid - Deadline → mid-February 2027 - Final decision → 25 member states, May 2028 - Outcome of the vote → official but consultative position On Tuesday, in Geneva, a collective of Geneva-based associations and political figures launched the cantonal constitutional initiative promoted by the Co-CERNés coalition. The aim is to put all major infrastructure projects linked to CERN to a popular vote whenever federal legislation provides for the canton to take a position. The text concerns cantonal opinions on CERN constructions or infrastructure requiring authorization. The result of the consultation would become the official position of the canton, but would retain a consultative nature: it would therefore not be a binding decision on the project. The launch follows the recent consultation procedure on the Future Circular Collider (FCC), described by the promoters as partial and as a denial of democracy. Christina Meissner, a Centre MP, accuses the Council of State of leaving the Confederation in charge of the entire dossier, reducing the canton’s effective role. > “This is about bringing the decision-making process back to the local and democratic level,” Meissner told the press. ### The disputed authority The promoters dispute the FCC’s having been placed under the authority of the Confederation, as is the case with airport planning or military infrastructure. In their view, this choice would exclude the application of cantonal powers in matters of building law. According to Co-CERNés, the project also risks jeopardizing sustainability objectives approved by the Geneva Grand Council and the population. Raphaël Mahaim, a Vaud national councillor from the Greens, considers it unlikely that a democratic rejection could be ignored by the Federal Council or the other CERN member states. Mahaim also considers invalidation of the initiative unlikely, recalling that similar mechanisms already exist in the Canton of Vaud for nuclear-related matters. The FCC is still under study: a 91-kilometer-long accelerator intended to succeed the LHC from 2045. The estimated costs are 15 billion francs, a figure that opponents believe could be higher. According to the coalition, it would be Europe’s largest construction site; the promoters fear heavy traffic for about ten years, millions of tonnes of excavation, the loss of agricultural land, and more than 100 kilometers of underground work. The concerns include cooling water, greenhouse gases, and consumption: the electricity required would be comparable to that of a city of several hundred thousand inhabitants. CERN presents the FCC as benchmark infrastructure for fundamental research. The decision will fall to the 25 member states in May 2028, barring postponements. To bring the initiative to a vote, 5’696 valid signatures are needed by mid-February 2027: the committee acknowledges the tight timeline. ## What changes for the canton and the federal dossier The practical point of the proposal is not the immediate approval of the FCC, but the way Geneva would formalize its position. The proposed rule would introduce a popular vote for every cantonal opinion concerning a CERN construction or infrastructure project requiring authorization. The result would remain advisory, but would become the official position of the canton. The change would therefore concern the local decision-making stage, not the final decision entrusted to the CERN Member States. ### From the opinion to the consultation The controversy arises from the relationship between local and federal powers. The proponents argue that the recent consultation on the FCC left the Geneva State Council with too little effective room to maneuver because the dossier was handled at the federal level. Their initiative seeks to bring that step back to the cantonal level through a vote, without eliminating the advisory nature of the outcome. The proposed model has a concrete consequence: the canton's position would be defined after a popular consultation rather than solely through the institutional opinion challenged by the coalition. A clear distinction nevertheless remains between the cantonal position and the decision on the project. The Federal Council and the other CERN Member States would not be replaced by the Geneva vote; Mahaim nevertheless considers it unlikely that a possible democratic rejection could be ignored. ### Territory, energy and timing To assess the dossier, the elements cited by the proponents are mainly territorial and environmental: heavy traffic for about ten years, millions of tonnes of excavation, loss of agricultural land and more than 100 kilometers of underground works. Added to these are the water required to cool the facilities, greenhouse-gas emissions and electricity consumption comparable to that of a city with several hundred thousand inhabitants. The source does not quantify the latter needs; the available figure is the estimated cost of 15 billion francs, a figure disputed by opponents. The timeline creates the main practical scenario. The committee must collect the signatures by mid-February 2027, while the 25 Member States are expected to decide in May 2028, barring postponements. The proponents admit that organizing a vote before that decision will be particularly tight. To separate the traffic issue from day-to-day expenses, the site offers the guide on costo della vita in Svizzera and the tools dedicated to mezzi pubblici. ## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to follow the procedure The sequence to follow is defined by four steps. Each has a different effect and should not be confused with the final decision on the FCC. This distinction helps follow the procedure without anticipating the effects of a vote. 1. Subject of the initiative. The committee proposes that every cantonal notice concerning a CERN construction or infrastructure project requiring authorization be submitted to a popular vote. This is the scope of the requested amendment. 2. Collection of signatures. To bring the initiative to a vote, 5’696 valid signatures must be collected by mid-February 2027. The deadline concerns the sponsoring committee and represents the first measurable step in the procedure. 3. Cantonal consultation. If the signature stage makes it possible to proceed to a vote, the outcome becomes the Canton’s official position. The source specifies that the result would retain an advisory character: the vote therefore expresses Geneva’s position without being binding. 4. CERN decision. The 25 member states are expected to take a position in May 2028, barring postponements. The committee acknowledges that the window for organizing a vote before that date will be particularly tight. ### Dates to keep separate For those who live or work in Switzerland, the clearest way to follow developments is to distinguish the signature deadline from the cantonal vote and the international decision. The first is the set deadline, the second is the expected popular vote, and the third remains up to the 25 CERN member states. These are not three equivalent stages: the consultation defines the Canton’s position, while the decision on the future accelerator remains part of the organization’s process. Any popular rejection should also be understood in this context. Mahaim considers it unlikely that it could be ignored by the Federal Council or the other member states, but the source does not present it as automatically binding. The practical point is therefore to follow two elements: the collection of the valid signatures and the timing of the vote in relation to May 2028. item.title: Switzerland: 10'500 pigs killed due to enzootic pneumonia
item.description: Health emergency in 14 cantons: over 10'500 pigs culled or slaughtered to stop the spread of a contagious lung infection.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Over 10'500 pigs culled or slaughtered - Measures in 60 farms in 14 cantons - Epidemic emerged on September 9 - The disease is not dangerous to humans ## Key facts - Disease → enzootic pneumonia (EP) - Outbreak → September 9 - Affected farms → 60 in 14 cantons - Total depopulation → 20 breeding farms in six cantons - Fattening farms → 40 in 14 cantons - Lucerne → 5'200 animals culled or slaughtered - Bern → 1'700 animals in three breeding farms - Compensation → for farmers who lose pigs by order of the authorities On September 9, enzootic pneumonia (EP), a contagious lung infection in pigs, emerged within a large inter-cantonal pig supply chain. The announcement was made by the Veterinary Service of the canton of Lucerne, which clarified an important point for the public: the disease poses no danger to humans. To stop the chains of transmission, the authorities ordered the complete depopulation of 20 breeding farms spread across six cantons. So far, the measure has led to the slaughter or culling of approximately 10'500 animals. At the 40 affected fattening farms, located in 14 cantons, restrictions on animal movements remain in force. The cantonal distribution shows a strong concentration in certain areas. Lucerne is the worst-hit canton: ten breeding farms and one fattening farm have been depopulated, for a total of 5'200 animals culled or slaughtered. In Bern, three breeding farms were affected, involving 1'700 animals. In Solothurn, 930 pigs were culled at two farms; others were slaughtered and approximately 1'200 young animals were exported. Other affected breeding farms were located in Schwyz, Thurgau and Vaud. The latter canton reported the culling of 950 pigs. In Bern, the restrictions imposed on four fattening farms were lifted following negative tests, while other farms are still under investigation. The restrictions imposed on breeding farms remain in force for the time being and may be lifted only after the barns have been completely cleaned and disinfected and have remained empty for at least ten days. The risk of spread is assessed for each farm. Veterinarians also visit neighboring farms to check the health status of the pigs. So far, there is no indication that farms outside the affected supply chain have been infected. The report does not quantify effects on prices, consumption or wages; it is therefore not possible to derive an estimate of costo della vita in Svizzera from the report for these data. ## Operational impact on the supply chain ### Breeding and fattening follow different rules The report clearly separates two operational pathways. For breeding farms, the measure is complete depopulation and the restriction remains tied to specific health conditions. For fattening farms, by contrast, the measure indicated is restrictions on animal movements, with checks still underway at some farms. It is therefore not a single provision applied in the same way throughout the supply chain. | Type of farm | Measure indicated | Next step | |---|---|---| | Breeding farm | Complete depopulation and restriction | Cleaning, disinfection and at least ten days with the barn empty | | Fattening farm | Restrictions on animal movements | Tests and investigations; in Bern, four restrictions were lifted after negative results | This comparison helps assess the situation farm by farm. A breeding farm cannot consider the restriction ended simply because checks have been carried out: the source also specifies complete cleaning and disinfection, followed by at least ten days with no animals. For a fattening farm, a negative test result has, in the reported case in Bern, already allowed the restriction to be lifted; other farms remain under investigation. The communication does not establish that the same result automatically leads to the lifting of the restriction in every canton. The presence of the supply chain in 14 cantons does not, according to the available data, amount to a generalized infection of Swiss farms. The risk is assessed individually, and veterinarians also inspect nearby farms. So far, no indications of contagion outside the affected supply chain have emerged. For those living in Switzerland, the health message is equally limited: the Lucerne Veterinary Service states that PE poses no danger to humans. The source does not, however, provide data on meat prices, availability in stores or consequences for the cost of living. Compensation should also be read without adding figures. It is provided for farmers who lose their pigs by order of the authorities, but no amount, calculation, timing or procedure is specified. It is therefore not a salary item: anyone who needs to distinguish this measure from their own income can consult the guide to busta paga svizzera, without attributing to the source information it does not contain. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## Operational steps ### What the communication indicates For pig farmers, the first indication is to remain vigilant and consistently apply biosecurity measures. The source does not list individual biosecurity practices, so it is not possible to turn this recommendation into a list of products, checks or documents. 1. Consider the risk of the individual farm. The authorities assess it individually, while veterinarians also visit nearby farms to check the health status of the pigs. 2. Comply with the restrictions on animal movements where they are still in force. The text links these restrictions to the affected finishing farms. 3. Await the outcome of the checks and tests. In the case reported by the canton of Bern, four restrictions at finishing farms were lifted after negative results, while others remain under investigation. 4. For breeding farms subject to restrictions, complete the cleaning and disinfection of the barns and keep them empty for at least ten days before a possible lifting of the restrictions. From an economic standpoint, farmers who lose their pigs by order of the authorities will receive financial compensation. The communication does not specify the amount, the calculation method, the deadline, the forms or the office to which an application should be submitted. Adding these details would mean going beyond the source. The same applies to any tax or accounting effects: they are not described and must not be inferred. For those who do not operate a farm, the news offers only two verifiable indications. PE was detected in an inter-cantonal pig-production chain and, according to the Veterinary Service of the canton of Lucerne, poses no danger to humans. In addition, so far there are no indications of farms outside the chain being infected. The source does not prescribe health-related actions for the population or announce general restrictions for consumers. This distinction avoids confusing a targeted veterinary measure with a general change for all residents. To separate compensation from employment income and make a personal estimate, use calcolatore stipendio. *Source: [swissinfo.ch](https://www.swissinfo.ch/ita/in-svizzera-10%27500-maiali-uccisi-per-malattia-polmonare/92176032)*

## TL;DR - The Swiss space industry generates approximately 330 million francs - The sector brings together approximately 120 companies and nearly 3000 employees - Artemis is preparing a lasting human presence on the Moon - The lunar economy could be worth 343-566 billion by 2050 ## Key facts - Space revenue → approximately 330 million francs - Active companies → approximately 120 - Employees → nearly 3000 - Increase in Beyond Gravity's turnover in 2025 → 12% - Estimated lunar economy in 2050 → 343-566 billion dollars The Swiss space industry is preparing for the industrialization of the Moon. According to Keystone-ATS, the industry generates approximately 330 million francs in revenue; including the scientific sector, the total reaches 400-600 million. There are approximately 120 active companies, and the sector employs nearly 3000 people. Swissmem, the association of the technology industry, describes the market as still young but growing strongly. ### A presence already integrated into European programs The Swiss Confederation is Europe's sixth space power and the seventh-largest contributor to the ESA, of which it is a founding member. Didier Manzoni, deputy director general of Apco Technologies, emphasizes that no European mission flies without important equipment manufactured in Switzerland. The company, based in Aigle (VD), has supplied equipment for the Orion spacecraft of the Artemis mission, the Ariane 6 rocket and all ESA programs, including ExoMars's Mars rover. The value of orders and the group's revenue remain confidential, while Manzoni describes the latter as increasing. NASA's Artemis program, which aims for a lasting human presence around and on the Moon, also involves Beyond Gravity, a subsidiary of Ruag International. For Orion, the group developed solar-panel orientation mechanisms. Its turnover, adjusted for the effects of divestments, increased by 12% in 2025, reaching 402 million francs; the Zurich-based group is investing in expanding production capabilities at several sites. EPFL is also a starting point for this industrial trajectory. Emmanuelle David, director of the EPFL Space Center, notes that investment in the lunar market is increasing. Pave Space, a start-up born out of EPFL and founded in 2024, raised approximately 40 million dollars in the spring, equivalent to 33 million francs, to develop vehicles intended to accelerate the deployment of satellites into orbit. David considers the fundraising one of the most significant in the European space sector. The transition from already-developed technology to a lunar presence remains the common thread: companies are now working on equipment and vehicles, while the Moon is identified as a future frontier. ## From the Artemis program to a supply chain with different timelines ### Two time horizons for businesses and workers For those who live or work in Switzerland, the decisive distinction is between the space economy that is already active and lunar industrialization that has yet to be built. The contracts mentioned concern equipment, mechanisms, life-support systems and energy transfer. They do not yet describe resource extraction on the Moon. Manzoni places industrial exploitation several decades away, while Sirin Orbital Systems points out that the contracts signed so far are limited. This time gap changes how businesses and workers interpret the situation. Matteo Madi expects strong demand growth by the end of the decade, linking it to the successful launches of major operators such as SpaceX's Starship. Deloitte's analysis, published at the end of August, instead measures the potential by 2050. These are two different time horizons: demand growth over the decade and long-term economic scale. | Horizon | Indication | |---|---| | Current situation | Technologies and contracts for space missions and future bases. | | End of the decade | Strong expected market growth according to Sirin. | | 2050 | Lunar economy estimated at between 343 and 566 billion dollars. | The estimates do not concern a single sector. Infrastructure for living and working on the Moon includes transport, energy, communications, mobility, construction and life-support systems. In a scenario of accelerated growth, this first market would be worth 282 billion dollars by 2050. Once the basic infrastructure has been created, national security, data and lunar services, new resources and materials, and production in space would add 284 billion. For Switzerland, the practical point is its position in the technology chain. Apco, Beyond Gravity, Sirin and Pave Space are cited for equipment, panel orientation, life support, energy and vehicles. Those who want to monitor the employment side can consult the annunci di lavoro, separating activities that have already been developed from prospects dependent on future space programs. The Artemis Accords also have a specific function. Launched in 2020 on the initiative of NASA and the United States and signed by several countries, including Switzerland, they lay the foundations for the exploration and exploitation of resources on the Moon, Mars and other celestial bodies. The principle cited by the source allows the extraction and use of resources without national appropriation: it is a framework for future activity, not an indicated start date. ## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## From news to a concrete fact-check To turn the news into a concrete fact-check, it is useful to follow an order that separates data, companies and timelines. The point is not to treat the Moon as an already mature market, but to understand which Swiss technologies are already linked to space programs and which depend on future developments. ### Four operational steps 1. Start with verifiable activities. Apco Technologies is linked to Orion, Ariane 6, ESA programs and ExoMars; Beyond Gravity to Orion; Sirin Orbital Systems to life-support systems and wireless energy transfer; Pave Space to vehicles intended to place satellites into orbit. 2. Separate technology from exploitation. The source describes solutions to make survival and energy distribution possible; it does not yet present operational industrial activities on the lunar surface. This distinction prevents every investment from being interpreted as extraction already underway. 3. Use the right time horizons. The end of the decade is the reference indicated by Sirin for demand growth; 2050 is the year in Deloitte's estimates; Manzoni speaks of several decades for exploitation. These are different reference points, not a single deadline. 4. Check the employment angle. Anyone considering a career change can explore the aziende che assumono and compare the available positions, without automatically attributing a lunar outlook to every role. To assess a report on resource use, the next check is the institutional reference mentioned in the article: the Artemis Accords, launched in 2020 and also signed by Switzerland. Their principle allows extraction and use without national appropriation; however, the source does not present them as a timetable for the start of industrial activities on the Moon. This distinction helps avoid confusing an international framework with an activity already underway. To check the location and type of activity, the source identifies Aigle (VD) for Apco, Zurich for Beyond Gravity and Sirin, and EPFL's Space Center in Lausanne as the scientific reference. The same analysis identifies the lunar south pole as a likely area for initial activities, thanks to the presence of ice, prolonged exposure to the sun and strategic terrain. The numbers must then be kept separate: revenue, employees, capital raised and estimates of the lunar economy measure different aspects. The text does not quantify individual salaries. item.title: New key projects for federal digital sovereignty
item.description: On October 1, 2026, the Chancellor designated the digital sovereignty workstation and EasyGov 2.0 as key projects; NEPRO leaves the category. Currently, 22 key projects account for more than half of civilian IT spending.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Two new projects become federal key projects. - Chancellor's decision: October 1, 2026. - EasyGov 2.0 lays the groundwork for the platform's stable development. - NEPRO leaves the key projects. ## Key facts - Decision → October 1, 2026 - Publication → October 6, 2026 - Location → Bern - New projects → workstation based on digital sovereignty; EasyGov 2.0 - Program excluded → NEPRO - Current key projects → 22 - Spending share → more than half of the ongoing civilian IT portfolio On October 1, 2026, the Federal Chancellor decided, after consulting the Conference of Secretaries General, to manage the program for a workstation based on digital sovereignty and the EasyGov 2.0 project as key projects. The announcement was published on October 6, 2026, in Bern. ### Initiatives concerned The workstation program was launched at the beginning of September by the Federal Chancellery. Its stated aim is to reduce dependence on foreign providers. The project concerns all departments and is of great importance for strengthening the digital sovereignty of the Federal Administration. EasyGov 2.0 is the project of the State Secretariat for Economic Affairs. The source attributes great strategic importance to it for the economy and the Confederation. Companies use EasyGov to easily access the services offered by numerous administrative units in all departments. The project creates the technical and organizational foundations needed for the platform's further stable development. The change also concerns NEPRO, swisstopo's new production systems program. Following the scaling-down it underwent in March 2026 and the marked improvement in the risk situation, NEPRO will no longer be managed as a key project. The announcement recalls the scope of the category. These are projects or programs of the Federal Administration in the area of digital transformation and IT that, because of their scope, strategic importance, complexity or associated risks, are of particular significance. For this reason, they require intensified management, coordination and oversight. The Swiss Federal Audit Office conducts systematic audits of key projects, while responsibility for individual projects remains with the competent departments and administrative units. In accordance with the Digitalization Ordinance, it is the Federal Chancellor, after consulting the Conference of Secretaries General, who determines which initiatives fall within the category. There are currently 22 key projects, and their total volume exceeds half of the expenditure of the entire portfolio of ongoing IT projects in the civilian sector. ### What changes operationally The transition to key-project status brings the two new projects under the intensified management, coordination and oversight regime provided for this category. The Swiss Federal Audit Office conducts systematic reviews. Responsibility, however, remains with the competent departments and administrative units: the classification strengthens oversight without replacing the project owners. For a company using EasyGov, the focus is the platform’s technical and organizational framework. The source says that EasyGov provides access to the services of numerous administrative units across all departments and that the project is preparing further stable development. No new functions, new access methods, costs or deadlines for companies are announced. The governance decision must therefore be distinguished from any potential changes in use, which the communiqué does not describe. | Initiative | Practical point indicated | Scope | |---|---|---| | Workstation | Reduction of dependence on foreign suppliers | All departments | | EasyGov 2.0 | Technical and organizational foundations for stable development | Companies and administrative units of all departments | | NEPRO | No longer managed as a key project | swisstopo program | The portfolio figure shows the scale of the decision: there are currently 22 key projects, and their volume exceeds half of the spending on ongoing civilian IT projects. However, the source does not assign an individual budget to the two new projects and does not allow costs or savings to be inferred. The NEPRO case also shows that the classification can be updated. The program will no longer be treated as a key project after the scaling-back in March 2026 and the improvement in the risk situation. In the broader economic context, those monitoring aziende che assumono can complement this reading with information on the business market. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ### Four-step verification 1. Start with actual usage. If a company uses EasyGov, identify the services it accesses through the platform and the administrative units involved. The source refers to numerous units in all departments, but does not list the individual services: the review must therefore be limited to what the company actually uses. 2. Separate access from the project. Note that the decision concerns the management of EasyGov 2.0 as a key project and that the project creates the technical and organizational foundations for stable development. The press release does not indicate a new registration, an additional document or a usage deadline to be applied to companies. 3. For a unit of the Federal Administration, verify which department or administrative unit remains responsible for the individual project. The classification does not transfer this responsibility: the text leaves it to the competent authorities, alongside intensified oversight and systematic checks. 4. Reconstruct the sequence of dates: launch of the program for the digital workstation at the beginning of September, the Chancellor's decision on October 1, publication on October 6, and NEPRO's downsizing in March 2026. This chronology distinguishes decisions already announced from any subsequent developments. For residents who do not manage business services, the press release does not describe an individual action, a form or a deadline. The operational information therefore consists in not attributing to the announcement any functions or procedures not indicated. Those following the market can also consult the annunci di lavoro. To complete the reading with a tool dedicated to personal finance, use the calcolatore stipendio. *Source: [admin.ch](https://www.admin.ch/it/newnsb/3zIflyRuW6a-)*

item.title: Natalie Rickli is taking time to consider a federal candidacy
item.description: Rickli, a Zurich cantonal councillor from the UDC, does not confirm her candidacy for the Federal Council and postpones her answer until after the autumn holidays; the deadline for applications is October 23.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - Rickli does not confirm her candidacy for the Federal Council - The Zurich councillor is considering a third term - The answer will come after the autumn holidays - The deadline to apply is October 23 ## Key facts - Person → Natalie Rickli - Role → Zurich State Councillor (SVP) - Position under discussion → succession to Guy Parmelin - Deadline → October 23 - Next statement → after the autumn holidays Natalie Rickli, a Zurich State Councillor from the Swiss People’s Party (SVP) and one of the favorites for the position that Guy Parmelin will leave vacant, has not confirmed a candidacy for the Federal Council. The position she has made public remains noncommittal: Rickli is not committing herself on a possible move to the federal government and is taking the time necessary to reflect. ### A dual interest In an Instagram post, the Swiss People’s Party politician wrote that she feels comfortable in the Council of State. In the same message, she declared herself ready to run for a third term. This willingness signals that she is ready to seek re-election to her Zurich post, but it does not resolve the question of Parmelin’s succession. The text indeed separates the two issues: on the one hand, the positive relationship with her current role and her willingness to run again; on the other, a federal candidacy that, according to the reported statement, requires further reflection. The news therefore records neither a yes nor a no. It records a pause in decision-making. The holiday period also helps define the timeline of the matter: the councillor is spending a holiday devoted to scuba diving. ### The date given The postponement was expressed in clear terms: > “Now I’m disappearing underwater, literally, and I’ll speak out after the autumn holidays.” The next statement is thus scheduled for after the autumn holidays, while the deadline for candidacies to succeed Parmelin is next October 23. The source does not give a more precise date for Rickli’s return to the issue and does not anticipate what her choice will be. For the national public, the key point to watch is the gap between a willingness to seek a third term on the Council of State and a candidacy for the Federal Council. Until Rickli speaks, both pieces of information must be considered separately. The news concerns this political choice and contains no measures on household income or expenses; a separate in-depth analysis is available at costo della vita in Svizzera. ## What waiting means The practical consequence of waiting concerns how the information is read, not an economic measure already announced. The source presents a possible federal-level succession, but does not describe a program, measure or change for residents. The reader can therefore distinguish what has already been stated from what remains open: Rickli wrote that she feels comfortable in the State Council and declared herself ready for a third term; regarding a candidacy for the Federal Council, she chose to reflect. ### Two time references The first reference is the promise to speak out after the autumn holidays. The second is the October 23 deadline for candidacies for Parmelin's succession. They are not the same information: the first describes when Rickli intends to speak, while the second indicates by when candidacies must be submitted according to the source. Bringing them together makes it possible to follow the matter without anticipating the outcome. | Question | Answer supported by the source | |---|---| | Is the candidacy confirmed? | No: Rickli remains noncommittal. | | Is a third term ruled out? | No: she has declared herself ready to run. | | When will she comment? | After the autumn holidays. | | What is the indicated deadline? | Next October 23. | This distinction prevents turning the willingness to serve a third term into a renunciation of the Federal Council, or interpreting the silence as a candidacy already decided. Neither conclusion is contained in the text. The source does not attribute positions to Rickli on other dossiers; automatically linking her possible candidacy to consequences not described would add extraneous information. The postponement does not, however, make it possible to establish whether Rickli considers one path more likely than the other. The text offers no elements with which to weigh the two options and records no further inclination: any prediction about the outcome would go beyond what is reported. For those living in Switzerland, the concrete fact is therefore the timing of the statement, not a change already announced. Anyone wishing to explore the daily balance separately can consult costo della vita in Svizzera, without confusing that topic with the candidacy that remains to be clarified. ## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ## How to follow the story For a reader who wants to stay updated without anticipating the decision, the most reliable method is to stick to the steps that the source makes verifiable. The text identifies a person, a possible post, a period for reflection, and a deadline. ### An essential checklist 1. Record the current status: Natalie Rickli is described as a Zurich cantonal councillor of the UDC. She should not be presented as already being a member of the Federal Council. 2. Separate the two forms of availability: her well-being in the State Council and her willingness to run for a third term do not amount to a confirmed federal candidacy. 3. Mark October 23: it is the deadline given for candidacies to succeed Guy Parmelin. The source does not provide another deadline. 4. Await the announced statement: Rickli said she would make her position known after the autumn holidays. This is the next explicit step in the text. 5. Assess only the published words: until a new statement, describe the candidacy as a possibility and do not attribute to the councillor a decision she has not communicated. This procedure is intended to avoid confusing three different elements: the political role Rickli currently holds, her willingness to run for a third term, and the possibility of a seat on the Federal Council. The source does not indicate forms, offices, requirements, or documents to submit; adding them would mean going beyond the available facts. The outcome of the deliberation also remains open. For readers nationwide, the economic links should be used as separate further reading, not as already announced consequences of the story. You can consult busta paga svizzera or dichiarazione delle imposte for topics other than the candidacy. item.title: Zurich Airport: record with 123'000 passengers
item.description: On Sunday, October 4, Zurich welcomed 123'000 travelers: a still-provisional record linked to the autumn school holidays in several German-speaking Swiss cantons.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - 123'000 passengers in Zurich on a single Sunday - The October 4 figure is still provisional - Autumn holidays in several German-speaking Swiss cantons - Final figures expected in mid-November ## Key facts - What → passenger record in a single day - Where → Zurich Airport - When → Sunday, October 4 - How many → 123'000 travelers - Data status → still provisional - Explanation → autumn school holidays in several German-speaking Swiss cantons - Update → final figures in mid-November - History → first runway in operation since June 14, 1948 On Sunday, October 4, Zurich Airport welcomed 123'000 travelers, the highest number ever recorded in a single day at the airport. The operating company announced the figure, confirming a report published by Tages-Anzeiger. The record is not yet final. A spokesperson clarified that the available figures are provisional; the final count will be released in mid-November. The wording already limits the scope of the news: the record concerns a single Sunday and, for now, is based on a count that still needs to be completed. The operating company linked the high passenger numbers to the autumn school holidays that began in several German-speaking Swiss cantons. The source therefore indicates a specific reason for the concentration of travelers: the holiday calendar in part of German-speaking Switzerland. To interpret the record accurately, it must be kept tied to the stated day and to the provisional nature of the count. It is not a description of an entire period, but the result reported for that Sunday. ### An airport with a national history Zurich Airport is described as Switzerland's most important airport. Its origins date back to the period after the Second World War, when aviation activities were transferred from Dübendorf (ZH) to the airport. The historical reference does not alter the record figure for Sunday, but recalls how aviation activities were transferred from Dübendorf after the war. The first runway entered service on June 14, 1948. That day, a Swissair Douglas DC-4 four-engine aircraft took off for London. This separation is also useful when writing the news: the airport's history explains its origins, while the record indicates only the volume handled on that day according to the available data. ## How to read the Swiss mobility record The data has two coordinates that need to be considered together: Zurich Airport and Sunday, October 4. The first identifies Switzerland's most important airport; the second indicates that this is a daily measurement, not an assessment covering an entire season. For those who live or work in the country, the news therefore offers a concrete way of interpreting it: in this case, the high passenger volume is linked to the school vacation calendar, which began in several German-speaking Swiss cantons. ### A number to use with caution The 123'000 travelers describe the scale of the day indicated by the operating company. On their own, they do not make it possible to turn the record into a forecast for every Sunday, a measure of annual traffic, or a comparison with other airports. These extensions would go beyond the reported data. The same company referred to the figures as still provisional: until the final numbers are released in mid-November, the term record must remain tied to the provisional wording. The explanation must also remain limited. The high passenger volume was attributed to the autumn school vacations that began in several German-speaking Swiss cantons. The data suggests looking at the cantonal calendar when analyzing days of peak mobility, but does not authorize presenting the same dynamic as uniform throughout Switzerland. ### A reference for those organizing their travel The information can be paired with practical tools without attributing to the record effects that the source does not describe. To navigate the options of mezzi pubblici, it is advisable to keep the historical data and travel planning separate. Those who need to assess expenses in foreign currency can use comparatore CHF/EUR, without confusing this tool with a consequence announced by the airport. The central point remains the quality of the measurement: one day, one provisional figure, one reason linked to vacations in several cantons. This precision makes it possible to use the news as a specific indicator of national mobility, without turning it into a broader statistic. ## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## Procedure for citing the record correctly Anyone who needs to mention the news in a communication, an analysis, or travel planning can follow four steps. The procedure does not change the source's content; it serves to ensure that the qualifications accompanying the data are not lost. 1. State the date. Write Sunday, October 4 and specify that it refers to a single day. The date prevents the record from becoming a generic reference to the airport's activity. 2. State the figure. Use the figure of 123'000 travelers welcomed by Zurich Airport. The word travelers should be linked to the airport and the stated day, not to an annual total. 3. State the status. Present the result as a record based on data that is still provisional. The spokesperson explained that the final count will be released in mid-November. 4. State the reported reason. Link the high turnout to the autumn school holidays that began in several German-speaking Swiss cantons, without expanding the explanation beyond what was communicated. ### Separate the data from the history If the news is accompanied by a fact sheet about the airport, it is advisable to keep the historical reference in a separate block. Zurich Airport was established after the Second World War with the transfer of aviation activities from Dübendorf (ZH). The first runway became operational on June 14, 1948; on that occasion, a four-engine Douglas DC-4 operated by Swissair took off for London. ### The final check In mid-November, when the final figures are released, the wording can be updated while keeping the date, quantity, and status of the data separate. The check must not anticipate the figures: it serves only to replace, when possible, the provisional indication with the final one. To plan travel, you can consult the public transport section. item.title: Rüegsegger UDC candidate for the Federal Council
item.description: The Canton of Schwyz puts forward André Rüegsegger to succeed Guy Parmelin: it is the first official candidacy following the announcement of his resignation at the end of the year.
item.content:encoded:
## TL;DR - The Schwyz UDC section proposes André Rüegsegger - First official candidacy after the announcement of the resignation - Rüegsegger has been a member of the Schwyz government since 2012 - The DFGP is indicated as a possible department ## Key facts - Candidate → André Rüegsegger - Party → UDC of the Canton of Schwyz - Age → 50 years old - Origin → Brunnen (SZ) - Cantonal government → since 2012 - Re-election in 2024 → second place, 37'989 votes - Department indicated → DFGP - First candidacy → after the announcement of the resignation at the end of the year The Schwyz section of the UDC has proposed State Councillor André Rüegsegger to the UDC's national search committee. It is the first official candidacy to emerge since President of the Confederation Guy Parmelin announced on Friday his intention to resign at the end of the year. The proposal comes from the Schwyz UDC section and is being presented to the national party as a candidacy to succeed outgoing Parmelin. Today's statement says that Rüegsegger has the ideal profile and age for the federal executive. Fifty years old, a native of Brunnen (SZ) and trained as a lawyer, Rüegsegger has been a member of the Schwyz government since 2012. Initially, he headed the Security Department; since 2020, he has been responsible for the Construction Department. In 2024, he was convincingly re-elected to the cantonal executive, finishing second overall with 37'989 votes. The report, however, concerns the proposal to the national committee, not a federal election result. The candidacy would also have a distinctive feature: Rüegsegger would be the first Federal Councillor from Schwyz in the federal executive. The source presents this as a possible first for the canton, alongside his biographical profile and experience in the Schwyz government. ### The political profile indicated by the party The UDC's cantonal president, Roman Bürgi, quoted in the statement, considers Rüegsegger particularly well suited to head the Federal Department of Justice and Police, the DFGP. According to the same statement, the State Councillor is also perfectly in tune with the national party. Another element highlighted in the profile is his position on the agreements with the EU. At the Swiss UDC assembly in January 2025, Rüegsegger argued that the package should be submitted to a double majority of the people and the cantons. In his view, the content and material significance of the treaties clearly place them at the level of the Constitution. Until now, his name had not appeared among the favourites for a Federal Council candidacy. Attention was focused in particular on Céline Amaudruz, Yvan Pahud and Nicolas Kolly, National Councillors from Geneva, Vaud and Fribourg respectively, or on a first candidacy by a German-speaking Swiss UDC woman: the St Gallen «senator» Esther Friedli or the Zurich State Councillor Nathalie Rickli. ## The political reading of the candidacy The Schwyz proposal does not amount to an appointment that has already been finalized. The fact recorded by the source is that Rüegsegger's name was sent to the national SVP's search committee, after Parmelin's announcement; for the time being, his status is that of a proposed candidate. This distinction is the first practical point for correctly understanding the news. ### Three aspects to keep separate | Aspect | Source information | Interpretation | |---|---|---| | Procedure | Proposal to the search committee | The candidacy is at the stage described by the source | | Background | He would be the first Federal Councillor from Schwyz | The canton is bringing a profile hitherto absent from the federal executive | | Positioning | FDJP and a double majority of the People and the Cantons | The candidacy is associated with these political elements | The territorial profile gives the candidacy a distinct feature. The source does not include Rüegsegger among the favorites mentioned so far; instead, it notes that attention was focused mainly on three SVP figures from French-speaking Switzerland, Céline Amaudruz, Yvan Pahud and Nicolas Kolly, or on a first candidacy by a German-speaking Swiss woman from the SVP, Esther Friedli or Nathalie Rickli. The comparison, therefore, concerns different backgrounds within the party. The second key is the possible department. Roman Bürgi identifies the FDJP as a suitable area for Rüegsegger; however, the source does not announce an allocation of departments. For the reader, this means distinguishing between an orientation expressed by the cantonal president and a federal decision that is not described. The significance of the candidacy is therefore political; the source does not report amounts or measures concerning costo della vita in Svizzera. The third key concerns agreements with the EU. The position expressed by Rüegsegger at the January 2025 assembly indicates his stance on the approval procedure: a double majority of the People and the Cantons. The text does not report the outcome of a vote on the package. The issue therefore remains an indicator of his political profile, not an outcome or decision already reported by the source. ## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to follow the story For those living or working in Switzerland, following this candidacy means above all distinguishing the steps already documented from the decisions that have not yet been described. The source allows for an orderly verification, without transforming a cantonal proposal into an appointment to the Federal Council. ### Four-step checklist 1. Check the status. The primary reference is the search committee of the national SVP: Rüegsegger was proposed there as a candidate. It must not be written that he is already a Federal Councillor or that the succession has been decided, as the source does not state this. 2. Verify the profile. The essential data are: 50 years old, origin in Brunnen (SZ), legal training, and presence in the Swiss Government since 2012. The chronology of departments completes the profile: security first, then construction since 2020. 3. Separate the cantonal result from the federal race. The 37,989 votes obtained in 2024 and the absolute second place refer to the confirmation in the Swiss executive. These are not votes for the Federal Council and should not be presented as such. 4. Read the European position as a political statement. The intervention at the SVP assembly in January 2025 concerns the double majority of people and Cantons on the package of agreements with the EU. This is a position attributed to Rüegsegger, not the announcement of a decision on the package. The source does not indicate a date for a possible election nor a procedure following the proposal. For this reason, the most useful update to look for will be the one that eventually clarifies whether the candidacy will remain in the party selection and how it will be compared with the names already mentioned.
